- Descript [C7], Screen Studio 4 [S4] and Tella [S11];
- Loom, on its Business + AI plan [S15];
- Prequel [S20] and Gling [C31].

Adobe lists Paper Edit in Premiere 26.5 [P4], though one verifier disputed it. Cap's changelog lists a word-level editor [S16] that a verifier could not confirm shipped.

Frame Job pulls ahead on terms and on depth:

- **Cost.** The on-device transcript costs nothing per minute. Descript meters media minutes and AI credits [D7] and draws complaints about speed [D8].
- **No model needed for retakes.** They are found by a deterministic comparison of neighbouring sentences, with no key.
- **Depth.** Every cut is an ordinary ripple edit in a full editor, with the audio chain, grading and graphics behind it, so restoring a cut is exact.
- **Agents for free.** The same word-to-timeline mapping already serves agents: `get_transcript` answers in timeline ticks, and `ripple_delete_ranges` is one undo step. "Drop the first take of every repeated line" therefore works the same by click or by chat.

Editing is the largest topic in one vendor's analysis of creator comments [D1].

**Builds on.** `DeviceTranscriptCache.swift` and `MediaTranscript.swift` (words cached per media in source ticks); AssemblyAI transcripts; `get_transcript` (`AgentServer+Transcript.swift`); `rc_project_source_map` (`speed_map.rs`, spec §11 SR-20) through speed, ramps and reverse; `ripple_delete_ranges` (`core/src/edit_time.rs`); `detect_fillers` and its lock, nest and transition rules.

**Effort.** L, as a short road map: the view with seek; delete as ranges; greyed, restorable words; the retake pass after its decision.

**Risks and what comes first.**
- Spec §11 TR-3 says a false start is never offered without a conversation. AI-6 and W-9 say no pipeline picks words to cut by meaning. A deterministic retake pass is such a pipeline, so it needs an amending §11 decision before code. Pauses and fillers already sit within TR-3 and TR-4.
- Restore is not one existing op. It is `insert_time` plus `trim_end` into the left clip's handle, grouped, or `add_clip` with a source range (next tier).
- On-device transcription kept 1 of 8 fillers in the owner's test (TR-7), so filler strike-through needs an AssemblyAI key.
- `MAX_CLIPS` (4,096) counts every clip, nested ones included, and each text cut splits every unlocked track. About 1,000 cuts over four tracks reaches the cap.
- The first fill of a whole-timeline view runs the recogniser at a few seconds per minute of speech. After that it is cached.
- A multi-hour transcript in one text view, kept in step with edits made elsewhere, needs care. The new pane needs a planned file split under the 600-line cap.

The companion item Punch in on cuts (next tier, S) hides the jump cuts this bet leaves.

### 2. Screen recordings with the cursor as data

**Pitch.** The recorder stops burning the pointer and click rings into the picture. Beside the movie it saves the cursor's path and image and every click. If the creator opts in, it also saves the shortcuts pressed. When the recording lands:

- zoom actions already sit on the action lane at each click and each burst of typing;
- the cursor is its own layer, which can be made bigger, restyled, smoothed or hidden when idle, and gets click ripples;
- each shortcut appears as a Keyboard keys overlay;
- long typing stretches can be sped up.

All of it is ordinary actions, clips and graphics that the creator can drag or delete. Recordings made before this ships, and imported screen videos, behave as today.

**Why it puts Frame Job ahead.** The polished-screencast category rests on cursor data:

- Screen Studio zooms where clicks happened [S2] and edits the cursor after recording [S3];
- Prequel stores the pointer as data [S19];
- Cap [S16], FocuSee [S18], Tella [S11] and Camtasia [S8] [S9] do the same.

Frame Job's recorder stores none of it, so Frame Job loses its own home segment to a recorder that costs about $29 a month [S7]. This bet brings Frame Job level on polish. It pulls ahead because those recorders are shallow editors and Frame Job is a full one. Its auto zooms are actions on a real timeline, next to grading, the audio chain, captions and graphics, and an agent can re-plan them ("zoom only on the clicks in the settings pane").

Being free is not unique by itself. OpenScreen is a free, MIT-licensed Screen Studio alternative with about 40,000 stars, archived after v1.5.0 [S23], and Cap sells a $58 lifetime licence [S17].

**Builds on.** `RecordingSetup.swift`, which sets `showsCursor` and `showMouseClicks` today; `add_zoom_action` (`core/src/edit_zoom.rs`); `add_speed_ramp`; the Keyboard keys graphic template; the recorder panel's grants; `recipe_layer.rs`; `MediaConsolidator` and relink.

**Effort.** L.

**Risks and what comes first.**
- Spec §11 (`recording.md`) decides three things this bet reverses: the cursor and click ring are taken as drawn and nothing is reconstructed; callouts stay out; a recording is ordinary media, with no source kind and no schema bump. The owner amends §11 first, as CAM-1 did for the camera.
- Shortcuts need the Input Monitoring grant, which `RecorderStatusItem.swift` deliberately avoids today. Key capture should be opt-in and record only modifier shortcuts by default. It must never record secure fields, and it must show plainly when it is on.
- The cursor must follow the screen clip's own transform and zoom actions. It has to be drawn as part of that clip's layer, or the two have to be nested with the zooms on the nest. A sprite on another track would drift.
- `NSCursor.currentSystem` is marked deprecated in macOS 27.0 in Apple's availability metadata, so a replacement is needed.
- The sidecar cannot be regenerated, so Consolidate and Relink must carry it.
- Timing can anchor on the screen's first-frame time, which the camera spike measured within 0.5 ms. Issue #370 is a microphone-offset problem and is not inherited.
- Motion blur on zooms needs sub-frame sampling and is out of scope.
- Code from AGPL-licensed recorders is not carried over, the same rule as for Concat.

### 3. Make Vertical Version

**Pitch.** File ▸ Make Vertical Version… writes a 9:16 or 1:1 version of a finished 16:9 edit. Each clip fills the frame and follows the face, person or salient region that Vision found on the Mac. It does this with ordinary eased x, y and scale actions the creator can nudge. In a screen recording made after bet 2, it follows the cursor instead. Captions re-lay for the short side, and graphics re-layout from the canvas size. A shot that cannot be cropped gets Add Blurred Background.

**Why it puts Frame Job ahead.** Subject-tracking reframe is table stakes. OpusClip [C11], CapCut [C4], Premiere [P21], Final Cut Pro for iPad [P17], Riverside [C9], Kapwing [C20] and Screen Studio [S1] all ship it, and auto-repurposing is the most-wanted creator AI feature in one survey [D2]. Frame Job pulls ahead on terms. CapCut moved Auto Reframe behind Pro in April 2026 [C4]. Here it is free and local, and the result is editable pan actions rather than a render. If the owner chooses linked versions (one cut, with a framing per shape), Frame Job is ahead of every rival, because their vertical copies drift from the master.

**Builds on.** `fill_scale` (`edit_fit.rs`); Add Blurred Background (`edit_background.rs`); word captions sized to the shorter side (`CaptionStyle.swift`); graphics that read `ctx.canvas`; actions (`edit_action.rs`); nests (`edit_nest.rs`); `set_canvas` (`edit_canvas.rs`); File ▸ Duplicate; the E9 Vision spike in `tools/proof/effects_spike/`.

**Effort.** M as a regenerated copy. L for linked versions, which need a canvas per version, framing overrides per clip and a format bump.

**Risks and what comes first.**
- Spec §1 lists auto-reframe as a non-goal, so a §11 decision must lift it first. The reason given there, heavy pixel work outside the one-pass compositor, no longer applies: the analysis runs offline and its output is actions.
- No two actions on one clip may overlap, of any kind. A clip that already carries an action (a zoom, a grade, a ramp) needs a wrapping nest, and a nest's canvas freezes at the size it was nested at.
- `set_canvas` does not rescale action end states. A screencast's existing zoom actions keep their 16:9 targets, and the planner must rewrite them.
- `MediaCacheLane` is a width-2 lane for audio decodes, so video analysis needs its own lane, cache kind and ledger rows.
- The planner should use face, human and saliency rectangles with tracking, not masks: the E9 spike found that foreground masks flicker on video.
- Two people in frame, a speaker leaving the frame, and shot changes inside one flattened clip each need a rule.

### 4. Find Clips

**Pitch.** Clip ▸ Find Clips…, run on an episode, a VOD or a finished edit, lists 10 to 30 candidates of 20 to 60 seconds. Each candidate shows:

- in and out points snapped to sentence ends;
- its length;
- a one-line reason, such as "laughter after the punchline";
- a preview.

There is no virality score. Make Short turns the checked candidates into vertical projects through bet 3. Each short is word-captioned, has fillers removed where a cloud transcript exists, and is queued for export.

**Why it puts Frame Job ahead.** Long-to-short is what OpusClip [C10] [C12], Riverside [C9], Submagic [C14] and Kapwing [C20] sell, all metered by credits. YouTube's own free tool covers only 10 countries and 7 languages [D9]. Frame Job pulls ahead in three ways:

- **Local signals.** Laughter, applause and cheering from Sound Analysis, the 10 ms loudness, speech spans and sentence ends are all measured on the Mac.
- **The creator's own key.** Ranking runs on the creator's Claude key, with no per-minute credits.
- **Real timelines.** Each candidate opens as an editable timeline.

A stated reason for each moment, rather than a score, answers the documented complaint that clippers cut in the wrong place [D16].

**Builds on.** `get_transcript` (timeline ticks); `ClipLoudness.swift` and the per-media loudness cache; `media_speech.rs`; `detect_fillers` and `ripple_delete_ranges`; caption Restyle with Replace; the Export Queue; the Assistant helper (`agent/`) and its price table; `set_range`.

**Effort.** M on top of bet 3. Without bet 3 it produces horizontal clips only.

**Risks and what comes first.**
- Ranking quality is the whole product.
- On-device FoundationModels has a 4,096-token context and needs Apple Intelligence turned on. It is a chunked, weaker fallback, not an equal path.
- Speaker labels exist only on AssemblyAI transcripts requested with speakers.
- No op copies a timeline range into a new project: `new_project` takes a path, and Duplicate copies everything. One is needed.
- Sound Analysis (`SNClassifySoundRequest` `.version1`, 303 labels on macOS 26.5.1, laughter, applause and cheering among them) is noisy on game audio and music beds.
- Long transcripts cost tokens, so show an estimate range before running.

### 5. Switch by Speaker, and read every audio track of a file

**Pitch.** The creator brings two to four cameras and a mic per person, lines them up with Synchronize Audio, and chooses Clip ▸ Switch by Speaker…. Frame Job cuts to whoever is talking, judging each mic's speech spans against that mic's own noise floor. It uses the wide shot during crosstalk and holds a minimum shot length. The whole switch is one undo step, and every cut is an ordinary split the creator can roll or re-pick. OBS multitrack files and multichannel recorder files import every audio track, not only the first.

**Why it puts Frame Job ahead.** Automatic switching is sold as AutoPod for about $29 a month [D14], as Resolve SmartSwitch in Studio [P8], and inside hand-off or metered tools such as Eddie [C32] and Descript. Premiere users have asked for it for years [D13], and video podcasts are the fastest-growing creator format [D10] [D11] [D12]. Frame Job already owns the hard audio half: drift-corrected sync, cached speech spans, the loudness cache, Match Audio, Enhance Voice, the leveller, a −16 LUFS target and stems. Adding the picture half makes it a free podcast editor. An agent can also re-run the switch with new rules, such as "cut to wide whenever both laugh".

**Builds on.** `AudioSync*.swift` (alignment as `move_clip` and `set_speed`); `SileroVAD.swift` and `media_speech.rs`; `audio_duck_speech.rs`; `ClipLoudness.swift`; `set_enabled` (a clip with its picture disabled is not decoded, per `nest.rs` `shows_video`); `ProjectDocument.performGroupedEdit`; `core/src/container.rs` and every `CompositionBuilder.firstTrack` audio caller.

**Effort.** M for speaker switching on stacked tracks plus every audio track. L for a multicam clip with an angle grid and live overrides.

**Risks and what comes first.**
- Spec §1 lists multicam as a non-goal, so a §11 decision must lift it, either narrowly (stacked tracks) or fully.
- Reading every audio track touches every `firstTrack(.audio)` caller: the builder, Silence, the isolation, ramp, voice and reverse renderers, and the transcription extract. It needs a format bump.
- Splitting linked picture and sound halves of three angles every 8 s for two hours gives about 5,400 clips, which is over the 4,096 cap. The switch should cut picture only and keep the mics whole.
- Mic bleed can mislead the switch, and one-mic shows need Vision mouth activity instead.
- Transitions decode both angles. Decoding three or four 4K angles has not been measured (see the next tier).
- Zoom and Riverside already deliver one file per participant, so the multitrack fix chiefly serves OBS and multichannel WAV.

### 6. Camera cutout and layouts

**Pitch.** The creator ticks Remove Background on a camera clip. Vision segments the person on the Mac, rendered in the background the way Reverse is. A Layout pop-up switches the camera at the playhead, with an animated move, between:

- corner bubble (circle or rounded);
- side by side;
- stacked for vertical;
- camera full;
- screen only.

"Hide camera while silent" fades the camera out during pauses. Text Behind Subject follows from cutout: a title sits between the person and their background.

**Why it puts Frame Job ahead.** This is mostly catch-up. Screen Studio 4 (cutout in beta) [S6], Cap 0.6 [S16], Tella [S11], Prequel [S19] and Loom [S13] shipped camera cutout or layouts in September and October 2026. Final Cut Pro [P14], Premiere [P2] and Resolve [P8] ship one-click subject masks. Frame Job's recorded camera is fixed in the bottom-right corner. It pulls ahead only in combination: layouts are actions any agent can write, the camera gets Frame Job's grading and LUT engine, and with bet 2 the whole screencast polish lives inside a full editor.

**Builds on.** Issue #124 and its E9 Vision spike; `ReverseRenderer`, `ReverseCache`, `BackgroundRender` and `MediaCacheLedger`; matte tracks (`recipe_matte.rs`); actions over transform, crop, corner radius and shadow; Add Background; the speech spans of the microphone media.

**Effort.** L.

**Risks and what comes first.**
- Edge quality on hair is a risk. Balanced person masks are 512×384 and likely need a refinement pass. Accurate masks run at 1.7× realtime and take 1.7 GiB per minute.
- Non-person masks flicker on video, so non-person cutout is for stills only.
- A mask on a Luma matte track has no link to the camera clip and drifts on trims, splits and speed changes. A per-layer mask with a format bump is the sound design.
- Issue #124's `texture(2)` binding is stale: looks now hold texture 2 and curves texture 3.
- The camera clip has no sound of its own, so hide-while-silent reads the microphone's spans through the microphone clip.
- Spec §1's ML non-goal, and issue #124's proposed decision D5, must enter §11 first.
- The 8-decoder budget is a warning, not a refusal. HLG projects need the mask in the right working space.

### The next tier

- **Proposals: play an agent's multi-step edit before it lands (M; Recipes later, also M).** Only Frame Job can do this cheaply. Handles are immutable. The export pin already renders a project that is not the current one. `performGroupedEdit` already makes one undo step from many. An agent's turn becomes a side chain the creator plays and compares A/B with the current cut, then accepts as one named step or rejects. This answers the 44% who want to review or undo and the 37% who want to see what the agent does [D4]. It amends spec §11 AI-10, which accepted ten Undos for a ten-call turn. It matters most once bets 1 and 4 produce agent-driven batches. Recipes come after Proposals and need three things: tool allow-lists enforced by the gate, because a shared recipe is a prompt-injection path; cost shown as an estimate range, because `pricing.ts` prices a run after it happens; and prompts served from `mcp-proxy`, because `core/src/agent.rs` is generic code.
- **Punch in on cuts (S).** Alternates scale between about 100% and 112% across cuts within one take, centred on the face, with `set_video` x, y and scale as one grouped step. It is free and exact, and needs no disclosure. Ship it right after bet 1's first phase.
- **Source ranges, skimming, In and Out, favourite ranges (M).** `add_clip`, `insert_clip` and `overwrite_clip` gain a source range, and `opTool` prints it into the MCP tools automatically. This is the precondition for placing a found moment and for a clean restore in bet 1. Add proxies only after a measurement shows a shortfall, under a recorded decision on a playback-only builder input.
- **Caption styles, brand kit and project templates (M).** Colour controls are safe under spec §11 W-10. Size and font changes need re-paging or a W-10 amendment. Per-word emphasis and emoji need a `model_words.rs` field and a format bump under W-2 and W-3. Whether emoji render correctly in HLG projects is unverified.
- **Publish polish slice (S).** A copyable 00:00 chapter list from chapter markers, checked against YouTube's rule [D21]; approximate platform safe-zone overlays [D24]; named platform export targets. Skip AI titles and thumbnails, which YouTube Studio is adding itself [C29].
- **Measure multi-stream 4K and multi-hour playback (S).** Bet 5 and any claim to lead depend on it. It is a measurement, not performance work.
- **`search_media` over cached transcripts (S).** The useful slice of a footage index. Build the Vision and Sound Analysis analysis inside bets 3, 4 and 6.
- **Merge the in-app tutorials after TU4 (S).** Creators arriving from CapCut need onboarding. The merge needs TutorialTargets rows for the audio road map.
- **Optical-flow slow motion, spike first (S, then M).** `VTFrameProcessor` accepts only 64RGBAHalf on this Mac, and its handling of HDR encodings is untested. Interpolated smooth cuts across a jump cut stay a spike, not a commitment.
- **WebVTT import (S); translated captions later (M).** A later phase of a caption road map, not a bet.

## Not worth chasing

| Item | Reason |
|---|---|
| Generative media: AI B-roll and video, avatars, voice clones, lip-synced dubbing | Nothing on the device can do it, so it means brokering credit-metered vendor APIs, the model Frame Job competes against. It carries disclosure risk [D25]. YouTube [C26] and Instagram [C28] now dub and translate for free. |
| Direct upload, scheduling, hosted share links, platform analytics | An open-source app with no backend cannot keep OAuth client secrets. A shared quota would cap all users together, and posting APIs need audits. Share links need a server. Bring-your-own storage is the only later form that fits. |
| Stock libraries; a template marketplace | These need licensing, curation and a backend. One developer cannot match CapCut's volume [C1] or MotionVFX inside Final Cut Pro [P15]. Agent-written graphics and `.fjgraphic` packages are the counter. |
| Eye-contact correction, face retouching | Apple has no public API for these on recorded video. They would need cloud or custom generative face models, with likeness risk and a per-frame cost the one-pass compositor cannot absorb. |
| Cloud sync, collaboration, mobile or iPad apps, Windows | Each needs a backend or a second platform. |
| Remote guest recording, live multi-camera capture | This is Riverside's moat [C9] and needs WebRTC servers. Import the per-guest files instead, and switch between them with bet 5. |
| A virality score | Creators distrust scored clips [D16]. A stated reason per moment is honest and controllable. |
| A standalone on-device footage index | The major editors shipped footage search within a year [P1] [P13] [P9]. Vision gives only fixed labels, so free-text search needs a bundled model whose licence is unverified. Build slices inside bets 3, 4 and 6, plus `search_media`. |
| Script to cut: a listening teleprompter that assembles takes | Teleprompters are common [S19] [S16]. Script-first recording suits a minority. `SpeechEngine.swift` is file-based today. The valuable kernel, retake removal, belongs in bet 1. |
| Translated captions and soft subtitle tracks as a bet | Platforms translate themselves [C26] [C28]. ADA Title II needs same-language captions, which Frame Job already makes. Platforms take the sidecar SRT and VTT files Frame Job already writes. |
| A publish kit as a headline | YouTube Studio is adding AI titles and title and thumbnail tests [C29]. The on-device model's context cannot hold a long transcript, and Frame Job already meets the loudness targets. Only the S slice is worth doing. |
| More MCP surface or a second agent mode as the headline | MCP became expected in 2026 [C6] [C13] [C21] [P10]. Every creator job shipped as ops becomes an agent tool anyway. |
| Stabilisation, for now | Phones stabilise in camera, and stabilisation mainly serves handheld vlogs. It is feasible later as a cached render. |
| Live-compositor motion blur | It needs several sub-frame passes, which breaks the one-pass compositor. |
| A plugin system | It contradicts the closed effect vocabulary (spec §11 R5-1, G-1) that preview and export parity and the proof suite rest on. |
| Pro finishing as headline features (Dolby Vision, synthetic depth of field) | Resolve and Final Cut Pro own these [P9]. Frame Job's colour and HDR already lead every creator tool. |
| Analytics-driven idea features | The platforms hold the data [C23] [C29]. |

## Decisions for the owner

1. **Lead segment.** Recommendation: creators who record themselves talking, meaning talking-head YouTube and screen tutorials (bets 1, 2 and 6). Then repurposing to shorts (bets 3 and 4), then video podcasts (bet 5).
2. **Which spec §1 non-goals to lift, and how far.**
   - Auto-reframe: needed for bet 3.
   - Multicam: narrowly, as speaker switching on stacked tracks, or fully, as a multicam clip with an angle grid (bet 5).
   - ML and heavy pixel work: needed for camera cutout (issue #124's D5, bet 6).
   - Optical-flow retiming and motion blur: stay out until a spike.
   - A plugin system: stays out.
3. **Which spec §11 decisions to amend before code.**
   - TR-3, AI-6 and W-9, so that a deterministic retake pass may strike words (bet 1).
   - `recording.md`: cursor as data, callouts, a source kind and a schema bump (bet 2).
   - AI-10, for Proposals.
   - W-10, for inspector caption styling.
4. **Shortcut capture.** Whether the recorder may ask for the Input Monitoring grant, with capture opt-in and limited to modifier shortcuts by default.
5. **Vertical versions.** A regenerated copy (M), or linked versions in one project, where one cut has a framing per shape (L, with a format bump).
6. **Language models.** Claude on the creator's key only, or Apple FoundationModels as a no-key fallback. FoundationModels needs Apple Intelligence on and has a context of about 4k tokens.
7. **Cloud.** Confirm that bring-your-own key stays the only cloud model. Then either accept that filler detection stays AssemblyAI-only (TR-7), or fund an on-device filler pass.
8. **Performance.** Allow one measurement of multi-stream 4K and multi-hour playback now, despite the features-first order, before bet 5 and before any claim to lead. Add proxies only if the measurement falls short.
9. **Real use.** Cut at least one real video per lead segment in Frame Job before or alongside the first bet, so the bets are tested against real work.
10. **Positioning.** Whether to present Frame Job to creators as free, open, on-device and credit-free. That position answers the most common switching triggers: price rises [C5] [S7] [D19], metered credits [D7] [P7] and content-licence scares [D18].

### The market: creator tools

# Creator survey: what would make Frame Job a leading creator editor

## Summary

This survey is dated 1 November 2026. It asks what would make Frame Job a leading editor for content creators. It draws on five inputs:

- an inventory of the tree;
- four research sweeps (creator tools, pro editors, screen and tutorial tools, creator demand);
- three strategists' proposals;
- the candidates merged from those proposals;
- adversarial checks of each candidate against the code, Apple's frameworks and the market.

Frame Job is already ahead of most creator tools on finishing: its audio chain, colour and HDR, codecs, and an MCP surface that covers the whole editor. It loses creators earlier, at the jobs that now define a creator editor:

- cutting a talk by its transcript;
- polishing a screen recording from the cursor;
- turning a horizontal edit into vertical shorts;
- finding the clips worth posting;
- switching podcast angles by speaker;
- cutting the presenter out of the background.

Agent access no longer sets a tool apart, because most AI-forward editors gained an MCP server in 2026. No rival combines what Frame Job has: a full editor whose every edit is a pure, undoable op, analysis that runs on the creator's Mac, and AI on the creator's own key with no credits.

The recommendation is to ship those creator jobs as on-device commands whose results land as ordinary edits on the timeline, in the order below. The rest is either table stakes to pick up later or not worth chasing.

## What Frame Job has

Frame Job is a native macOS editor for Apple Silicon, macOS 26 or later. It is a Swift/AppKit app over a Rust core, Apache-2.0, with no account and no backend. As of 1 November 2026 it has the following.

- **Editing.** One kind of track. Move, trim, slip, roll, rate-stretch, split, lift, ripple delete, insert and overwrite. Nests. Picture and sound linked for J- and L-cuts. Markers with a chapter flag. A second preview window. Every edit is one undo step through one mutation point, and a refused edit says why in the rule's own sentence.
- **Picture.** Transform, crop, blend modes, chroma key, spotlight, obscure regions, text with reveals, shapes with gradients, blurred backgrounds, and matte tracks that let any clip cut the track behind it. Actions animate almost every property, including speed, which is how speed ramps work. 13 transitions, and Zoom to Region for screencasts.
- **Audio.**
  - A per-clip chain: voice isolation, EQ, hum and noise reduction, gate, a phrase-level leveller, de-esser, compressor and true-peak limiter.
  - Enhance Voice, Match Audio, Normalize to LUFS, Duck by Speech, and Synchronize Audio with drift correction.
  - Track compressor and limiter, a live loudness meter, stems, and a −1 dBTP master on every export.
- **Clean-up.** Remove Silences (on-device Silero VAD), Remove Filler Words (AssemblyAI word timings; cloud-only), and `get_transcript`. The Assistant cuts false starts when asked.
- **Captions.** On-device or AssemblyAI transcription. Subtitles plus five word-by-word styles and three looks. SRT and WebVTT export; SRT import.
- **Colour and HDR.**
  - Grading: wheels, curves, hue curves, looks, .cube LUTs, adjustment clips with qualifiers, and four scopes.
  - Log footage: Apple Log (detected on import), S-Log3, V-Log and Canon log.
  - HDR: HLG projects with HLG, HDR10 and SDR deliverables, on a 16-bit float compositor.
- **Graphics.** Sandboxed JavaScript modules that return SVG per frame, 23 bundled templates, shareable `.fjgraphic` packages, and agents that write new graphics.
- **Recording.** A display or a window through ScreenCaptureKit, with system audio, a separate microphone file, click rings, pause and resume, a camera beside the screen (bottom-right), and voice-over.
- **Export.** H.264, HEVC (10-bit and with alpha), AV1 and VP9 through bundled encoders, ProRes, audio formats and stems, GIF, APNG and stills. An Export Queue, embedded chapters, and loudness targets of −14 and −16 LUFS.
- **Agents.** 106 product tools over a local socket (one per edit, plus app-state tools), the bundled `framejob-mcp` helper, and `render_frame` so an agent can look at its work. An in-app Assistant runs on the creator's own Anthropic key and shows its spend.

### Where it is already ahead

- The whole editor is exposed as MCP tools printed from the core's own op table. Every agent edit is an undo step shown live, and `render_frame` lets an agent check its work.
- Its audio chain is deeper than any creator tool surveyed: a leveller, de-esser, true-peak master, LUFS targets, stems, Synchronize Audio with drift correction, and Duck by Speech.
- Colour management and HDR deliverables (HLG, HDR10, an SDR version) and log support. Creator tools lack these.
- Codec breadth: AV1 and VP9 with bundled encoders, VP9 and HEVC with alpha, ProRes 4444, and WebM and MKV import without re-encoding.
- A programmable motion-graphics engine whose templates agents can write.
- Open source with bring-your-own key and on-device processing first: no credits, no subscription, no upload of footage.

### What creators ask for

- **Editing is the biggest time sink.** One vendor classified 27,555 comments on 44 creator-education channels. Editing and production was the largest category, at 21.4% of actionable comments, ahead of monetisation at 15.6% [D1]. This is one vendor's analysis, not a survey.
- **Most work alone, and repurposing is wanted.** In Adobe Express's survey of 384 US video creators (December 2025), 86% work solo. The most-wanted new AI features were auto-repurposing (19%), instant platform-specific edits (14%) and help while filming (14%) [D2].
- **AI use is near-universal, but cost and training worry them.** In Adobe's 2025 Creators' Toolkit (more than 16,000 creators, 8 countries), 86% use generative AI. High cost is the top barrier, at 38%, and 69% worry their content will train AI without permission [D3].
- **They want control over agents.** In Adobe's 2026 report, 85% say the final decision must stay with the creator. Among creators who want more agent independence, 44% want to review, edit or undo at any point, and 37% want to see what the agent is doing and why. 57% say AI output usually needs moderate or extensive editing [D4]. Epidemic Sound found 94% use AI and 89% feel pressure to [D5].
- **Video podcasts are big and the picture edit is still manual.**
  - YouTube reports over 1 billion monthly podcast users [D10]. Spotify says more than 500 million users have streamed a video podcast [D11]. Edison found 57% of Americans 12+ have both listened to and watched a podcast [D12].
  - Automatic angle switching has long-open Premiere idea threads [D13] and is sold as AutoPod for about $29 a month [D14].
  - Descript users ask for multicam export to Final Cut Pro and Premiere (181 votes) [D6].
- **Descript frustrations.** The top requests are regenerating speech in more languages (753 votes), an iOS/iPadOS app (417), transcription in more languages (400) and strip silence (192) [D6]. Reviewers report slow scrubbing and long exports [D8]. Plans moved to media minutes plus AI credits with no rollover [D7].
- **Captions.** Premiere's animated-caption request has about 416 votes, and users round-trip to CapCut [D15]. A verifier counted about 380. Either way, the request is for animated word captions, which Frame Job already has.
- **Auto-cutters are distrusted.** Riverside Magic Clips is faulted for cutting where a thought ends rather than where the energy peaks [D16]. Gling sometimes cuts good takes [D17].
- **What makes creators switch tools:**
  - price rises and forced subscriptions [C5] [D19] [S7];
  - content-licence scares [D18];
  - stability regressions [D20];
  - metered AI credits [P7] [D7].
- **Platform rules a tool can check.**
  - YouTube chapters start at 00:00, need at least three, and each must be at least 10 s [D21].
  - Apple Podcasts asks for about −16 LKFS with a true peak at or below −1 dBFS [D22].
  - Spotify video podcasts want H.264, 16:9 and Rec.709 with stereo AAC, and HDR is tone-mapped to SDR [D23].
  - No platform publishes safe-zone figures, and third-party figures conflict [D24].
  - YouTube requires disclosure of realistic synthetic content but exempts colour fixes, background blur, captions and audio repair [D25].
- **Platforms build the simple cases themselves.** YouTube's own clips tool suggests moments only in 10 countries and 7 languages [D9]. Twitch is building vertical streaming (beta) and Auto Clips with captions (waitlist) [D26].

## The bets

The bets are ranked by how many creators each reaches, how often they would use it, and how far it puts Frame Job ahead rather than level, discounted by effort and risk.

Every bet has the same shape. Analysis that Frame Job already caches, or that macOS provides on the device, feeds a planner. The planner writes edits the core already knows how to make. Each result is therefore an ordinary undo step on a real timeline, and each command becomes an MCP tool that the Assistant and outside agents can run with no new agent work.

Effort is build effort (S, M, L, XL), never lines of code.

| Rank | Bet | Effort | Serves |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Transcript tab | L | Everyone who records themselves talking |
| 2 | Screen recordings with the cursor as data | L | Screencasts, tutorials, courses, product demos |
| 3 | Make Vertical Version | M (copy), L (linked versions) | Everyone who posts shorts |
| 4 | Find Clips | M on top of 3 | Podcasters, long-form YouTubers, streamers |
| 5 | Switch by Speaker, and every audio track | M | Video podcasts and interviews |
| 6 | Camera cutout and layouts | L | Screencasters, talking heads, streamers |

Bets 1 and 2 remove the two points where talking creators and the home segment give up. Bets 3 and 4 complete the long-to-short loop. Bet 5 takes the podcast format on the strength of the audio chain. Bet 6 closes the presenter-camera gap.

### 1. Transcript tab: cut by deleting words, with retakes found for review

**Pitch.** A Transcript tab shows the timeline's words in timeline order. The word being spoken is highlighted during playback, and clicking a word moves the playhead to it. The creator selects a sentence and presses Delete, and that span ripples out of the video as one undo step. Cut words stay greyed in place and can be restored.

A review pass strikes through long pauses and, where an AssemblyAI transcript exists, filler words. After the §11 decision below, it also strikes earlier takes of each repeated line and false starts. One click removes everything struck, as one undo step. Words inside a nest or a transition overlap show as not editable, with the reason.

**Why it puts Frame Job ahead.** On its own this brings Frame Job level. Editing by transcript ships in:

- Descript [C7], Screen Studio 4 [S4] and Tella [S11];

# Road map "audio" — a professional audio toolset (tiers A and B)

**Opened 2026-10-30** (AP0), when the owner answered the five choices below ("Yes, lift scopes,
and allow Apple's built-in audio effects", then "OK" to each of the rest): AU-2…AU-4, and spec
§1's audio non-goal lifted. The brief
is `designs/audio-survey.md` (its tiers A and B; tier C is not in this road map). The worktree is
`.claude/worktrees/audio-updates`, branch `worktree-audio-updates`, from `33eeed0`. Decisions are
AU-2 onward, in `designs/spec/11-decisions/audio.md` (AU-1, the ×32 volume ceiling, is built).

## Goal

Frame Job's audio today is a creator-tier strip: volume, fades, clip-extent ducking, pan, mono,
a compressor, steady-noise reduction, peak Normalize, and an export loudness target that only
turns the mix down (`docs/guide/audio.md`, `docs/guide/export.md`). After this road map a person
can take a quiet, noisy or uneven voice recording to a delivery loudness with one command and
then refine it: loudness they can see and target, a true-peak limiter, EQ, a gate, a de-esser,
hum removal, voice isolation, parameters that move over time, J- and L-cuts, track faders and
buses, stems, speech-aware ducking, matching, scrubbing and voice effects. Every control has its
MCP mirror, as every control does today.

## What it delivers first

The owner's recording, `samples/Rode-usb-mic.m4a`, peaks at −18.6 dBFS with an integrated
loudness of −44.7 LUFS. Peak Normalize and the export's loudness target both stop near −27 LUFS
(the survey's §2), because neither can reduce a peak. **After AP2, one Normalize press in
Loudness mode takes it to the chosen target (−16 LUFS by default) at −1 dBTP.** After AP6, one
Enhance Voice press also cleans it: the high-pass, the noise floor in the pauses (about
−36 dBFS once lifted, 65 % of the file), the compressor set from the clip's own level, the
limiter and the target.

## The owner's choices (answered 2026-10-30: all five as recommended)

Recorded as AU-2 (choice 1), AU-3 (choices 4 and 5) and AU-4 (choices 2 and 3). The owner,
on the rest: "We'll address other questions as we progress. If builds can be run in multiple
lanes, do so."

1. **Scope (spec §1).** Lift "no EQ" and "no mix buses", and allow Apple's own audio units
   inside Frame Job (as `AVAudioUnitTimePitch` already runs for speed-ramp audio). Hosting
   third-party Audio Unit plug-ins stays out of this road map (tier C, C5). *Recommended.*
2. **Normalize's default.** Keep peak normalize as the button's default until AP2's limiter
   lands, then make **Loudness** the default with Peak a choice beside it. *Recommended.*
3. **The default loudness target.** −16 LUFS integrated at −1 dBTP (voice platforms and
   podcasts), with −14 (YouTube's playback reference) and −23 (EBU R 128) as quick picks.
   *Recommended.*
4. **Own DSP or Apple's units for the live stages.** Frame Job's own DSP for EQ, gate,
   de-esser, hum notch and limiter, written beside the compressor: live in the tap,
   deterministic, testable against analytic responses. Apple's units only where Frame Job cannot
   write its own: ML voice isolation (`AUSoundIsolation`) and E8's voice effects, both rendered
   offline as speed-ramp audio is. AP0's spike S1 confirms or overturns this. *Recommended.*
5. **One fixed chain order, not a user-ordered list.** Channels → high-pass and EQ → hum notch
   → isolation or noise reduction → gate → de-esser → compressor → limiter, each stage off by
   default and inert when off. A closed vocabulary like every other effect (§11 R5-1), and the
   order an engineer would choose for voice. *Recommended.*

Asked later, at the phase that needs them (each has a recommendation there): how the volume
line is edited (AP8), the split-edit model (AP9), track processing in the preview and the stem
format (AP10), and where speech spans live for ducking (AP11).

## The orchestrator's defaults (each one the owner can change)

- **Working arrangement:** this worktree is the integration branch; each phase is built
  through litecode in a lane of its own, gated, committed, rebased onto the integration branch
  one at a time and gated again there, as codec-export (CX-11) and grading (GR-25) merged
  phase by phase. Merging into main is done from the main checkout.
- **Lanes (the owner's "multiple lanes"):** after AP0, at most three at once, split by the
  files they touch. **Lane A, the voice block:** AP1 → AP2 → AP3 → AP4 → AP5 → AP6, then AP8
  and AP14, which build on its stages. **Lane B, editing and playback:** AP9 → AP13 → AP7
  (the meter after AP1 has landed, since both read `Loudness.swift`). **Lane C, the mix:**
  AP11 → AP10 (after AP2 has landed: both work in the export's float gain stage) → AP12
  (after AP3). A lane whose next phase waits on another lane's phase waits; it never builds
  against an unlanded one.
- **Collisions between lanes:** each phase numbers its decisions in its own block (APn's
  AU-n0…, AU-2's note), and a format bump is provisional until its phase lands: the
  integrator renumbers it (and its `schema_vN.rs`) when another lane landed one first.
- **Agent parity:** every new property is a `set_audio` key, every new command a tool, every
  new answer readable through `get_project`.
- **Proof currency:** exports decoded to PCM and measured by the proof's own arithmetic
  (`phase5_proof.py`'s BS.1770 and 4× true-peak oversampler), synthetic fixtures with known
  answers, and the owner's samples where present. What only ears can judge is a row in
  `docs/manual-checks.md`.
- **Samples:** the owner records the survey's §6 list. A phase uses a sample when it exists and
  a synthetic fixture otherwise; no phase waits for one.
- **Persisted fields** carry serde defaults and bump the format (`core/CLAUDE.md`); an older
  project opens unchanged and sounds the same.

## How it fits the tree (at `33eeed0`)

- **The clip strip runs in a tap, before the fader.** `AudioTap.swift` (595) puts one
  `MTAudioProcessingTap` (PreEffects) on each composition audio track and schedules each clip's
  settings by span (`AudioDSPSpan`). `AudioDSP.swift` (**890, over the cap**) holds pan, the mono
  fold, the compressor (default threshold −18 dB) and noise reduction, real-time safe. Volume,
  fades and ducking come after the tap, as the core's envelope played as volume ramps
  (`core/src/audio.rs` 537, `audio_duck.rs` 136). **A new live stage sees the clip at its
  recorded level**, so a level-relative stage (limiter, gate) must be told the clip's gain.
- **The preview has no post-mix insert; the export does.** One tap per input, already used by
  the meter (`LevelMeter.swift` 400, which sums per-track peaks as an upper bound, not the mix).
  The export measures a 32-bit float mix and gains it in `ExporterAudioGain.swift` (179); its
  write pass still decodes 16-bit integers (#86).
- **Offline renders have a pattern.** Speed-ramp audio renders into `cache/ramp-audio/` through
  `RampAudioRenders` (a serial queue, owners, a wait in the export, dry while pending).
- **Loudness exists once.** `Loudness.swift` (**674, over the cap**) is BS.1770-4 for the
  export; `ExporterLoudness.swift` (211) its measurement pass.
- **The model.** `AudioProps` lives in `core/src/model_props.rs` (551), checked by
  `props_check.rs` (526) and clamped by `actions_clamp.rs` (386); pan, mono, compressor, noise
  reduction, duck and keep pitch are BASE-only (`InspectorBinding+Writes.swift`'s
  `structural(audio:)`), and only volume, mute and the fades animate.
- **Caches.** Peaks, sync features and speech (Silero VAD) per media, on the cache lane
  (`MediaCacheLane.swift`); a loudness cache would be a fifth beside them.

## Phases

| Phase | Survey items | What a person gets |
|---|---|---|
| AP0 | — | Scope lifted, the spike's answers, the files split |
| AP1 | A2, A8 (readout) | A clip's LUFS shown; Normalize to a loudness |
| AP2 | A1, A13 | A true-peak limiter; the export reaches its loudness; 24-bit |
| AP3 | A3, A7, B7 | EQ and high-pass, hum removal, channel selection |
| AP4 | A5, A6 | Gate/expander, de-esser |
| AP5 | A4, B4 | Voice isolation; de-reverb if isolation does it |
| AP6 | B1, B3, B8 | Enhance Voice; the leveller; clean-up when a voice-over lands |
| AP7 | A8 | Live LUFS and true-peak meter |
| AP8 | A9 | Every audio parameter animates; the volume line on the clip |
| AP9 | A10 | J- and L-cuts that keep sync; reversible Detach |
| AP10 | A12, A11 | Track faders, track and master processing, stems |
| AP11 | B2, B9 | Ducking by speech; fade and crossfade shapes |
| AP12 | B6 | Match one clip's level and tone to another |
| AP13 | B5 | Audio while scrubbing |
| AP14 | B10 | Voice effects (E8, #123) |

AP1–AP6 are the voice block, in the order the owner's recording needs them. AP7 onward is the
mixing block and can be reordered freely; only AP12 needs AP3, and AP6 needs AP2–AP5.

### AP0 — scope, the record, the tolls and the spike

- **Decisions:** AU-2 (the scope, from choice 1), AU-3 (the chain, choices 4 and 5), AU-4 (the
  loudness defaults, choices 2 and 3). Spec §1's non-goal sentence rewritten; this road map
  opened.
- **Tolls, each a pure move landed and gated alone:** `AudioDSP.swift` cut at its MARKs (the
  compressor and noise reduction into their own files, the chain kept); `AudioTap.swift`'s
  schedule and parameters (its first two MARKs) out of the tap; `Loudness.swift` cut below the
  cap; `AudioProps` and its vocabulary out of `model_props.rs` into a new `model_audio.rs`.
- **Spike S, its rule fixed before its run, its record here:**
  - **S1 — own DSP or Apple units, live.** A biquad EQ and Frame Job's limiter against
    `AVAudioUnitEQ`, `AUNBandEQ` and `AUPeakLimiter` driven inside the tap: byte-identical
    exports run twice, preview against export, CPU per track at eight stages, latency.
  - **S2 — voice isolation.** `AUSoundIsolation` rendered offline over the owner's recording:
    speed against real time, latency, determinism across runs, the pause floor and the speech
    band against the shipped noise reducer, and whether it reduces reverberation (B4's
    question), on a reverberant sample if one exists.
  - **S3 — tracks and the master in the preview.** Whether one composition audio track ever
    carries two timeline tracks; the error of a track chain run per composition track during an
    overlap (zero for linear stages, measured for dynamics); the options for a preview master
    limiter (none and say so, per-track, or an offline premix); rebuilding the true mix from the
    taps for a LUFS meter.
  - **S4 — a loudness cache.** K-weighted 100 ms block energies per media: size, build time on
    a 20-minute file, and integrated LUFS over any window against `Loudness.swift` measuring an
    export of the same window (agreement within 0.1 LU).
- **Acceptance:** `make gate` after each toll; the spike's verdicts recorded here.

### AP1 — loudness you can see and target (A2, A8's readout)

- A per-media loudness cache (`cache/loudness/<id>.bin`, S4's format) on the cache lane after
  peaks, current by `CacheStamp` like the others.
- The Volume section reads the clip's integrated loudness (gated, over the window that plays)
  and its true peak beside the Gain row.
- Normalize gains a **Loudness** mode: a target in LUFS, each clip of a selection to the same
  target, which is what "match these clips" means. Until AP2, a clip whose peak would pass the
  ceiling stops short and says where it landed, as the volume ceiling does today.
  `normalize_clip` gains `mode` and `target_lufs`.
- **Proof:** exports of normalised fixtures measured by the proof's BS.1770 within ±0.5 LU;

- **Proof:** exports of normalised fixtures measured by the proof's BS.1770 within ±0.5 LU;
  the owner's recording; a selection of two levels landing equal.

### AP2 — limiters, and an export that reaches its loudness (A1, A13)

- A **clip limiter** stage in the tap: lookahead, 4× oversampled true-peak detection, a ceiling
  in dBTP. Because the fader is downstream, the stage is told the clip's gain (decision AU-n:
  the base volume, with fades and ducks only ever lowering it), and its lookahead is a lead
  like noise reduction's (SY-25).
- The **export:** a float decode before the gain (#86, closing it), a master limiter in the
  float write pass so the loudness target limits instead of capping, and an `audio_bits` choice
  of 16 or 24 on WAV and AIFF.
- Loudness Normalize uses the clip limiter, so the owner's recording reaches −16 LUFS at
  −1 dBTP. If choice 2 says so, Loudness becomes the button's default here.
- **Proof:** every export's true peak at or under its ceiling by the proof's oversampler; the
  loudness target met within ±0.5 LU on `phase5_proof.py`'s crest fixture, which today lands
  quieter; a 24-bit file decoded with its low bits used; the owner's recording.
- **Manual check:** no pumping or distortion on speech and on music.
- **Built in two parts, by size.** Part 1: the clip limiter, `audio.limiter` (format 30), its
  Limiter section and `set_audio` key, and Loudness Normalize through it as the default
  (AU-20…AU-26; its record below). Part 2: the export's float decode (#86), the master limiter
  in the float write pass and `audio_bits` (AU-27 on).

### AP3 — EQ, hum removal and channel selection (A3, A7, B7)

- **EQ:** a high-pass with a slope, a low-pass, low and high shelves and a number of parametric
  bands (set at AP3), with voice presets (rumble cut, de-mud, presence). An EQ section in the
  Sound sub-tab with the response curve drawn.
- **Hum:** notches at 50 or 60 Hz and its harmonics, depth and harmonic count.
- **Channels:** both, left only, right only, swapped, before the mono fold, so a mic recorded
  on one channel of a stereo file plays at its level.
- **Model:** `audio.eq`, `audio.hum`, `audio.channels`; format bump; MCP keys.
- **Proof:** tones and sweeps through each band against the biquad's analytic response
  (±0.1 dB); notch depth at each harmonic; a channel pick sample-identical to its source channel.

### AP4 — gate, expander and de-esser (A5, A6)

- A downward **expander/gate** sharing the compressor's envelope follower: threshold relative
  to the clip's measured level (AP1), ratio, range, attack, hold, release.
- A **de-esser:** a compressor keyed on a high band (frequency, threshold, range).
- **Model, inspector, MCP** as AP3; format bump.
- **Proof:** a tone burst over noise, the pause floor lowered by the range and the burst
  untouched; sibilant noise bursts reduced in band and the voice band untouched; the owner's
  recording's pause floor.

### AP5 — voice isolation (A4; B4's verdict)

- **Isolation** by `AUSoundIsolation` (S2), rendered offline per clip window into
  `cache/isolated/` on the ramp-audio pattern: an Amount (wet/dry), dry while pending, the
  export waiting for its render, re-rendered when the window or the file changes.
- **De-reverb (B4):** if S2 measured reverberation removed, it is this control and the guide
  says so; otherwise B4 is filed with tier C and the measurement.
- **Proof:** the render aligned with the dry clip within a sample (cross-correlation); the pause
  floor and the speech band against the dry clip; dry while pending; an export that waits.
- **Manual check:** artefacts on the owner's voice at Amount 100 % and 50 %.

### AP6 — Enhance Voice, the leveller, and clean-up when a voice-over lands (B1, B3, B8)

- **Enhance Voice** (Clip menu, a button in the Sound sub-tab, an `enhance_voice` tool): reads
  the clip's loudness, its peak and the noise floor over the VAD cache's non-speech spans, then
  writes ORDINARY settings a person can see and change — high-pass, isolation or noise
  reduction, gate, de-esser if the high band is hot, a compressor set from the clip's own
  level, the limiter and the loudness target. One undo step; pressing it twice changes nothing.
- **Leveller (B3):** a slow gain-rider stage for a speaker who moves on and off the mic, off by
  default, turned on by Enhance Voice when the speech's short-term loudness range calls for it.
- **At record time (B8):** a recorder setting, "Enhance the microphone when it lands", applying
  Enhance Voice to the Microphone clip after the landing, as its own undo step (AU-68).
- **Proof:** the owner's recording to −16 LUFS ±0.5 at −1 dBTP with its pause floor lowered;
  idempotence; one undo step; a voice-over that lands enhanced.
- **Built in three parts, by size, as AP2 was.** Part 1: Enhance Voice itself — the measurements,
  the rules, the loudness cache's high band (version 2), the volume solved on the clip rendered
  through its own chain for Enhance and Loudness Normalize alike (the owner's answer,
  2026-10-31), the Measuring Sound sheet, the button, Clip ▸ Enhance Voice and `enhance_voice`
  (AU-60…AU-65; its record below). Part 2: the leveller, `audio.leveller` (a format bump) — after the
  owner's answer of 2026-10-31 a gain curve made ahead of time from the clip's loudness and
  speech and applied with no state in the tap — its section, and Enhance turning it on from the
  speech's short-term loudness range (AU-66, AU-67; its record below). Part 3:
  "Enhance the microphone when it lands", the recorder setting and its `UserDefaults` key,
  applied after the landing as its own undo step (AU-68, AU-69; its record below).

### AP7 — live loudness and true-peak metering (A8)

- Momentary, short-term and integrated LUFS and true peak while playing, over the true mix
  (S3's method), with a reset; the per-clip readout is AP1's.
- **Proof:** a probe compiled from `app/Sources` fed EBU Tech 3341's test signals, each within
  its tolerance.

### AP8 — every audio parameter animates; the volume line (A9)

Built in two parts once the owner answered the question below with (a), actions (2026-10-30,
AU-80): **AP8a** the volume line, app-only (AU-80…AU-84); **AP8b** every other audio parameter as
action ends through the same model (AU-85…).

- **AP8b:** pan, EQ gains and frequencies, gate, de-esser, compressor and limiter settings,
  isolation's Amount and the leveller's target as action ends; the tap's schedule carries
  per-parameter ramps from the core, not one constant per span. Switches (a stage on or off)
  still change at an action's end, as booleans do (§5.4).
- **AP8a, the volume line:** each clip draws its envelope over its waveform; dragging it edits the
  level. **Asked at AP8:** edit through actions (a point is an action's end, which keeps §2's
  "Actions, not keyframes"; recommended) or add keyframes (lifting it). Answered (a).
- **Proof:** the line drawn where the plan's ramps are (AP8a); exports of an animated pan and EQ
  against analytic gains (AP8b).

### AP9 — split edits (A10)

- J- and L-cuts that keep sync, and Detach Audio made reversible (Attach Audio).
- **Asked at AP9:** a LINKED pair — Detach's two clips carrying one link id, moved, cut and
  deleted together, with ⌥-drag trimming one half alone (recommended: it fits one kind of
  track, and an audio lead on its own track cannot collide with "overlap is a transition") —
  or one clip whose audio window extends past its picture.
- **Proof:** core tests of every edit on a linked pair; exports with the audio leading and
  trailing the picture by a known amount.

### AP10 — tracks, buses and stems (A12, A11)

- A **track fader and pan** in the header and the Track menu (an envelope term in the core, as
  a track's mute is).
- **Track and master processing** by S3's verdict, asked at AP10: the master limiter in the
  export at least; in the preview, as S3 found possible, or said plainly where it differs.
- **Stems:** each track, or a chosen set, as its own file in one export; **asked at AP10:**
  separate files (recommended) or a multitrack movie if S3 measured it to work.
- **Proof:** fader arithmetic on an export; the stems summed against the full mix (a null within
  quantisation when no master dynamics run).

### AP11 — ducking by speech, and fade shapes (B2, B9)

- **Ducking by speech:** the ducking clip's speech spans from the VAD cache, with pre-roll, hold
  and release, drawn as the envelope it makes. **Asked at AP11:** spans persisted on the media
  (a detected field, as Camera Log's is; recommended, so the plan stays a function of the
  project) or handed to the plan by the host.
- **Fade and crossfade shapes:** linear, S-curve, +3 dB and −3 dB, sampled by the core like an
  eased action.
- **Proof:** the plan's ramps against fixture spans; exports of each fade shape against its
  formula.

### AP12 — match one clip to another (B6)

- **Match Loudness** to a reference clip (AP1's measurement) and **Match EQ:** the reference's
  and the target's average speech spectra fitted to AP3's bands. A command and a tool.
- **Proof:** pink noise tilted by a known EQ matched back within ±1 dB a band.

### AP13 — audio while scrubbing (B5)

- Short grains of the mix at the scrub position while the playhead is dragged, off when the
  drag stops; the design is set at AP13 against what AVFoundation allows.
- **Proof:** a probe of the grain scheduler. **Manual check:** the feel, and no clicks.

### AP14 — voice effects (B10, E8)

- E8 as designed and measured (`designs/adr/effects-survey.md`, #123): sixteen kinds as fixed
  chains of Apple units rendered offline, with an amount and a pitch. Closes #123.

### AP0's record (2026-10-30)

**Landed.** `9e47f56`: the survey, this plan, AU-2…AU-4 and spec §1's audio non-goal lifted. The
tolls, each a pure move gated alone (PASS 307, 246, 243 and 136 s) and checked line-identical
against `9e47f56`: `c67ccee` (`AudioDSP.swift` 890 → 368; `AudioCompressorStage.swift` 158,
`AudioNoiseReductionStage.swift` 376), `54e4649` (`AudioTap.swift` 595 → 328;
`AudioTapSchedule.swift` 273), `a0eb094` (`Loudness.swift` 674 → 511; `ExportLoudness.swift` 168,
which `phase5_chrome.py`'s section 9 now compiles too), `6a51bfc` (`model_props.rs` 551 → 459;
`model_audio.rs` 114); the map entries `fec5132`.

# 1. What this is

A screencast editor without a recorder — and, since road map 3,
a recorder of the SCREEN, and since §11 CAM-1 of a camera beside it or on its
own, whose output is ordinary media. Open one or
more video files from disk, arrange them on layered tracks over a fixed canvas, trim,
split, annotate, animate, and export. Mac only, Apple Silicon, macOS 26+.

The bar is a balance: enough to make a real cut with text,
shapes, transitions and simple animation, without Final Cut's magnetic
timeline, roles, multicam, scopes, or a plugin ecosystem.

Deliberate non-goals: multicam, color grading beyond
per-clip controls (§11 GR-1: tier 1 of grading — tone, adjustment clips,
looks, LUT import, an ungraded switch and one luma waveform — is in, kept by
the owner's verdict of 2026-10-10, and tier 2's scopes, colour wheels,
curves and qualifiers beside it, GR-10…GR-13; tier 3's HDR→SDR conversion
and camera log are in, GR-15, GR-16; the HDR road map's HLG timeline, its
HLG, HDR10 and SDR-version deliverables, HDR scopes, the PQ peak, Canon Log
2 and 3 and opt-in linear-light blending are in, HD-1…HD-17; a wide-gamut
working space for SDR projects is not wanted, GR-20; tier 4's vectorscope zoom,
hue curves, the blend between curves of different point counts and the
qualifier's cleanup blur are in, GR-24, GR-31…GR-35, while an Offset
wheel, a qualifier on picture clips, 1,024-level scopes and a histogram
behind the curves are not wanted, GR-27…GR-30), a plugin system (a clip may
draw itself from a JavaScript module in its package, road map 10; nothing
else is scriptable — §11 G-1),
motion blur, stabilisation, optical-flow retiming and auto-reframe (heavy
pixel work or ML, outside the compositor's one-pass shape — road map 2 §4),
any platform but macOS. **Screen recording was on this list until road map 3
reversed it** (§11): the app records a display or a window through
ScreenCaptureKit into a file it then imports exactly as File ▸ Open would —
paused and resumed from the menu bar, each stretch its own file and its own
clip; callouts reconstructed after the fact stay out. **Camera recording
was on it too until §11 CAM-1** (road map "camera-recording") reversed it: a
camera alone or beside a screen recording, each its own file and clip.
**Audio beyond what shipped was on it too until §11 AU-2** (road map
"audio", 2026-10-30) lifted it: EQ, track and bus processing, and Apple's
built-in audio units are in, beside Frame Job's own DSP; hosting
third-party Audio Unit plug-ins stays out, under the plugin system above.

**The opening flow is the point.** File > Open on a `.mov` or `.mp4` (or a
drop on the Dock icon, or the welcome window's Open Video…) creates an
*untitled* project sized to that file, with the file as the first clip on
Track 1, ready to cut. Save then writes a `.framejob` package next to the
source. The app is also the Alternate handler for movie, audio and image
types so Open With… works from the Finder.

# Spec §11 — decisions: The Assistant (road map 12)

Part of spec §11, *Decisions made — do not re-litigate*. The index of every decision is
[`README.md`](README.md).

The road map that made these is closed; its condensed record is `designs/adr/roadmap-12-assistant.md`
(the original is `archive/roadmap-12.md`, whose §4 made them, amended by the user's answers
in §6).

- **AI-1 — The assistant is a bundled helper, and the app never calls Anthropic itself.**
  `Contents/Helpers/framejob-agent` is Bun-compiled from `agent/` on the Anthropic TypeScript
  SDK's Tool Runner, as Rasterize builds its own (road map 12 §1, §2). It is the one TypeScript
  in the product; G-11 ("no TypeScript") governs graphic Modules and is untouched. The Swift
  side uses `Process`, pipes and GCD, so W-8's `async` confinement holds. Risk accepted: Bun in
  every `make app`, and a nested executable of H1's size, signed separately.
  **Amended by NM-5** (rename R0): `Contents/Helpers/reelcut-agent` is now
  `Contents/Helpers/framejob-agent`.
- **AI-2 — The helper owns no tools; every call goes through `AgentServer.execute` by way of
  one lane.** An `AgentLane` holds one lock around every tool call from either caller, the MCP
  trampoline and the assistant session; the trampoline's call to it is the only wiring change
  in the frozen `AgentServer.swift`. The lane routes a call to main, or leaves it on its own
  queue for the `offMainTools` (§3a), and the session never takes the lock on main, because an
  off-main tool holding it waits for main (§3b). The same gate, parity check, refusals and undo
  steps apply; there are no assistant-only tools. Risk accepted: one lock serializes both
  callers, so a long off-main call (`export`, up to 3600 s) holds the other.
- **AI-3 — The catalog and the gate are prepared at launch, not at `start()`.**
  `prepareCatalog()` builds the catalog, runs `noteArguments` and runs the parity check;
  `start()` and the assistant both call it, because the gate treats a tool it has no schema for
  as taking nothing (§3c). A `make test`-reachable probe proves that an assistant call with an
  argument succeeds in a launch WITHOUT `-AgentServerEnabled`. Risk accepted: the catalog is
  built and parity-checked at every launch, whether used or not.
- **AI-4 — The Assistant is the inspector's fourth tab: Clip, Media, Document, Assistant.** This
  amends the sharp handoff's "no assistant panel" line, which was about Rasterize's parts
  rather than this feature (§3e); it gets a menu item with a key (spec §9). The user chose the
  tab to start and may move it to a floating window after trying it (§6.1), so the pane holds
  only views: the session, the transcript's storage and the pending confirmation live outside
  it, and a move is a new host for the same views. One conversation per window; the session
  lives on `EditorViewController` and survives tab switches, pane rebuilds and inspector
  collapse (§3h). Risk accepted: the transcript gets only the inspector's width, and showing it
  hides the other tabs.
- **AI-5 — The assistant edits its own window's project.** The lane pins the call's document
  the way `callScope` pins the scope: a per-call `callDocument` that `targetDocument` checks
  first, cleared by a `defer`. A `project` argument naming a DIFFERENT open project is refused
  by name, because an untitled project has no path and a window switch mid-turn would move the
  next edit (§3d). Risk accepted: one conversation cannot edit a second open project.
- **AI-6 — W-9 governs automatic styling, not a person's request.** No PIPELINE picks words by
  meaning. The assistant writes a caption's text or style only because the person asked it to
  in the conversation, and each such edit is an ordinary undo step (§3g). Risk accepted: a
  person may ask for emphasis by meaning, which no pipeline may do.
  **Amended 2026-10-22, by TR-5:** the same holds for cutting words. When the person asks,
  the assistant may choose words to cut by their meaning (a false start), reading them through
  `get_transcript`, a clip's words in timeline times that never makes a network call. It
  proposes, then makes ordinary undoable cuts; no pipeline picks words to cut by meaning.
- **AI-7 — What the assistant may not call, and what it must ask about first.** Withheld: the
  dev tools, always (V-1: they are not in Distribution, and the assistant sees one catalog in
  both builds); `record_screen`, always, because recording is a person at the Record button;
  and `transcribe` with the cloud engine, refused with R6-2's sentence and pointing at File ▸
  Generate Captions…. Ask first: `export`, `export_captions`, `save_project` and
  `consolidate_media`, because each writes files where the model chose (§3f, §6.3). Such a call
  is NOT run when the helper asks; the transcript shows a confirmation row naming the tool and
  where it writes, with Allow and Deny, and the helper's `tool_request` simply waits, so the
  helper is unchanged. Deny answers the call as an error, "The person declined: …". Stop,
  Clear, closing the window and a dead helper all answer a pending confirmation as declined.
  An MCP caller is never asked: the rule belongs to the assistant's lane, not to the tool. Both
  lists are one table in one file, with a "withheld" or "ask first" column and a reason on
  every row; the helper never sees a withheld tool, and the lane refuses one if it is called
  anyway. Risk accepted: recording and cloud transcription stay menu-only, and every file
  written costs a click.
  **Amended 2026-10-01, by #40**: `close_project` is withheld, always: closing a project
  closes the window the conversation lives in (AI-5).
  **Amended 2026-10-22, by TR-10**: `transcribe_for_fillers` is withheld, always, with R6-2's
  reason, pointing at Clip ▸ Remove Filler Words…, which shows what is uploaded and what it costs.
- **AI-8 — The key is the person's own, and is R6-5 and R6-12's key in everything but the
  vendor.** It lives in `SecretStore` under `anthropic-key`; the one override is
  `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, read only as R6-5 amended says. It is never a tool argument, a launch
  argument or an answer, and is handed to the helper on stdin only (§1, §3i). R6-9's
  `-RCSecretFolder` keeps proofs away from the person's file. R6-5's "integrated AI offering"
  is THIS, and it does not unblock C2 (#125), which still needs the caller's identity. Risk
  accepted: a `0600` file rather than the Keychain, for R6-5's measured reason.
- **AI-9 — History is append-only, and end-of-turn compaction is the one rewrite.** Rasterize's
  rule, for the same reasons: Opus 5.5 rejects replayed thinking after an edited prefix, and an
  unchanged prefix keeps the cache warm; compaction runs only at the end of a turn, past a
  threshold (§1). Risk accepted: old renders stay in context until compaction.
  **Amended 2026-10-01, by AI-20 (#151)**: compaction can be turned off or its threshold
  changed in Settings, and with "Clear old tool results" on, the API's clearing is a second
  rewrite — of what the model sees in a request past 150 000 tokens, possibly mid-turn, not of
  the helper's history. Each clearing breaks the prompt cache once.
- **AI-10 — Each tool call the assistant makes is its own undo step,** exactly as an MCP call
  is. A turn is not grouped, and the Edit menu names the step as it would for the same call
  from MCP (§6.4). Risk accepted: a ten-call turn is ten Undos.
- **AI-11 — The default model is `claude-opus-5-5` at medium effort.** The model is a person's
  setting, chosen in Settings' Assistant pane; like the key, no tool reads or writes it
  (§6.2). Risk accepted: the costliest default, paid with the person's key.
- **AI-12 — A tool call that arrives during a live gesture waits for mouse-up, then runs.** It
  applies to every caller, MCP and the assistant alike, because the lane (AI-2) is shared.
  "Live" means any open `ProjectDocument.isLiveEditing`: a timeline, canvas or inspector-slider
  gesture. A waiting call is never refused and never lost; before this, a call run between two
  ticks of a drag answered ok and was then undone by the next tick (#144; road map 12 §7 D2).
  The call lands above the gesture's own undo step. It is reversible: the wait is
  `AgentLane.onMainWhenIdle` alone. Risk accepted: a call, and the lane's lock with it, waits
  as long as the mouse is held down.
- **AI-13 — The assistant's one base-URL override is `RC_ASSISTANT_BASE_URL`, and with it set
  no key file is opened.** The helper's `api_base` comes from this environment variable alone
  (the shared `protocol.ts` calls it "an environment variable of its own"; A0's F and T rows
  used it). Plain `http` is accepted only for a loopback host, as R6-9 allows for AssemblyAI;
  any other value refuses the session by name. This is AI-8's R6-9 made explicit:
  `-RCSecretFolder`, from the argument domain, names the folder of `anthropic-key`; with the
  override set and no `-RCSecretFolder`, NO `FileStore` is built and the store is an empty
  `MemoryStore`, so the person's file is never read; the store is read first and
  `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` second (R6-9 (d)). A variable rather than the argument domain because a
  variable cannot be persisted in the app's defaults, which is R6-9 (c)'s reason. Risk
  accepted: a person who exports it sends their environment's key, and only that, to the
  server it names.
- **AI-14 — A selection change that is not a click on a clip leaves the Assistant tab
  showing; a click on a clip still shows Clip.** The inspector's switch to Clip on a changed
  selection (`InspectorViewController.refresh(isLive:)`) runs only from the Media and Document
  tabs. The assistant's own calls change the selection mid-turn, and a tab that jumped to Clip
  under the person would hide the reply and the ask-first row they are waiting on.
  `clipPicked()` — a click on a clip in the timeline or canvas — still shows Clip from any
  tab. Risk accepted: a selection made by an MCP caller or a menu item while the Assistant tab
  shows does not bring the clip's properties forward; a click does.
- **AI-15 — The window's live context rides on each person message; the system prompt is fixed
  for a session.** `AssistantSession.send` writes the person's text behind a
  `<framejob_context>` block (`AssistantLiveContext.swift`): the project's name and path, the
  open nest, the playhead and the selection, as they are at send time. The system prompt, the
  tool-search guide and the compaction instructions are written once, in `configure`, and never
  change for the session. `configure` is the helper's only system channel and `agent/` is one
  diff with Rasterize (#147); a system prompt that changed per turn would break AI-9's
  unchanged prefix and the prompt cache; and the playhead and selection change between turns.
  Risk accepted: about sixty tokens on every message, and the block is the state at send time,
  so after its own edits the model re-reads with `get_project`.
  **Amended by NM-5** (rename R0): `<reelcut_context>` is now `<framejob_context>`.
- **AI-16 — Stop stops a running `export` or on-device `transcribe`; any other running call
  finishes.** Each call the session submits carries a per-call token through
  `AgentLane.submit`, and Stop cancels the running call's token. The lane answers a call whose
  token is already cancelled when it takes the lock "Cancelled by the user." without running it.
  A running `export` links its token to `Exporter.cancel()`, which only sets flags (G-17's
  cross-thread hazard does not arise; the writer removes its part-file), and an on-device
  `transcribe` links it to its `Transcriber.CancelToken`, the transcribe sheet's own path; the
  model gets the tool's own sentence ("The export was cancelled.", "The transcription was
  cancelled."). Before this, Stop only stopped the helper's turn, and an export in flight wrote
  its file to the end (#149). Risk accepted: `render_frame`, `render_graphic`, `import_media`
  (an opt-in ffmpeg conversion included), `save_project`/`new_project` and the main-thread tools
  run to their end; Clear, closing the window and a dead helper still let a running call finish,
  its result dropped, as before; cloud `transcribe` is withheld (AI-7) and not linked.
  **Amended by #326**: `export` answers at once, so Stop no longer reaches it; a queued export
  stops by `cancel_export` or the Export Queue's Cancel.
  **Amended 2026-10-23, by TR-11**: Stop also reaches `get_transcript`'s on-device run, linked to its `Transcriber.CancelToken` the same way, and the model gets "The transcription was cancelled."
- **AI-17 — The transcript is one selectable text, and the composer is multi-line with K-2's
  Return** (issue batch B18, #153, #154). The transcript is one non-editable text view: the
  entries in order, one "\n" between them, so a selection and a plain-text copy cross entries;
  a reply that is still extending edits only its own range. The layout dump reads the entries
  as parts the transcript names (id `assistant.entry.<kind>`, text, rect), since one text view
  has no subview per entry. The composer grows from one line to five, then scrolls. A bare
  Return or keypad Enter (⇪ allowed) sends while idle and beeps otherwise; it never answers a
  question. Return with ⇧, ⌘, ⌥ or ⌃ inserts "\n", K-2's rule through the same
  `TextEditKey.route`; nothing is routed while an input method has marked text. Tab and ⇧Tab
  move focus, as the single-line field's did; they never type a tab into the message (amended
  by K-4: they, and a Return that sends, hand the keys back to the editor). The
  composer's typing undo is its OWN `UndoManager`: ⌘Z in the composer undoes typing, and typing
  never lands on the document's stack, never dirties the document and never enters
  `registerUndo`'s grouping (AI-10, app/CLAUDE.md's Undo); a programmatic set of its text (a
  send, the dev tools' pane path) drops that undo history. "No undo" was not chosen: a text
  view that does not register undo still answers ⌘Z through the window's manager, which is the
  document's, so ⌘Z while typing would undo a project edit. Risk accepted: accessibility sees
  one text area, not one element per entry; and the scroll to the newest line still runs on
  every change, so it can move a drag-selection during a streaming reply.
- **AI-18 — A proof lowers the end-of-turn compaction threshold with the dev-only launch default
  `-RCDevAssistantAutoCompact <tokens>`; the shipped threshold stays 300 000** (issue batch B26,
  #161). `AssistantConfiguration.settingsJSON()` sends `autoCompactTokens` (300 000, AI-9) as
  `configure.settings.auto_compact_tokens`; a build with `FRAMEJOB_DEV_TOOLS` (V-1) sends the
  knob's value instead when it is present, read from the ARGUMENT domain alone
  (`AssemblyAIConfiguration.argument`). A value that is not a whole number of 1 or more is named
  on stderr and ignored. It replaces nothing else, and a Distribution build does not compile it.
  Why: a 300 000-token context means a body far past row H's 256 000-byte bound
  (`assistant_prompt_eval.py`) and dollars of cache writes for every run, while on-demand
  compaction has no trigger or minimum of its own (the SDK's `BetaCompactionConfig`), so at 1
  every turn ends compacted and one short conversation proves the whole path against the real
  API (`assistant_compaction_proof.py`). Risk accepted: the proof shows summaries of tens of
  thousands of tokens, not of 300 000; and #151's person setting, when it lands, will not remove
  the knob.
  **Amended 2026-10-01, by AI-20 (#151)**: the knob replaces the person's threshold (300 000
  unless changed in Settings), and wins even with compaction turned off.
  **Amended by NM-6** (rename R0): `REELCUT_DEV_TOOLS` is now `FRAMEJOB_DEV_TOOLS`.
- **AI-19 — While the window's assistant waits on an ask-first question, the Assistant tab's
  title wears a dot, whichever tab is showing** (issue batch B47, #152; the owner's choice,
  2026-09-30: "badge the Assistant tab's title"). The dot is its own view over the strip
  (`InspectorTabBadge`), just right of the title, in the accent colour; `PanelTabsView` is not
  forked (Controls.swift's sync rule). It shows exactly while the window's session has a
  `pendingQuestion`, set by `assistantRefresh()`, which runs after every question and answer, so
  it goes off at Allow, Deny, Stop, Clear, a key or model change, the helper's exit and the
  window's close. It shows on the Assistant tab too, so it depends on the session alone. It is
  passive: it takes no click (a click on the tab only shows the tab) and no key, so Return still
  never answers (AI-17, K-2); the tab never switches itself and no note appears. Risk accepted:
  a collapsed inspector shows no dot (no strip is on screen), and another window shows nothing —
  a question in one window draws no attention in the others.
- **AI-20 — The chat settings are the person's, in Settings' Assistant pane, and a change
  reaches an open conversation without ending it** (issue batch B48, #151; the owner,
  2026-09-30: "Yes, make these settings available to the user"). They are Rasterize's two:
  "Compact when context reaches N tokens", on, N a whole number from 20 000 to 900 000, 300 000
  by default (AI-9); and "Clear old tool results past 150,000 tokens", off, acting past the
  helper's fixed `CLEAR_TRIGGER_TOKENS` (150 000, `agent/src/main.ts`). They live in
  `UserDefaults` under `FrameJobAssistantAutoCompact`, `FrameJobAssistantAutoCompactTokens` and
  `FrameJobAssistantClearToolResults` (`AssistantChatSettings`); like the model, no tool reads or
  writes them (AI-11's reason). A stored value outside the range reads as 300 000; a typed one
  beeps and the field shows the stored value again. `configure.settings` carries
  `auto_compact_tokens` (null when compaction is off) and `clear_tool_results`. A change applies
  at once, with no Save, and is written to every open session as `{type: "settings"}`: it ends
  nothing, unlike a key or model change. The helper reads the threshold at each turn's end and
  fixes clearing when a turn starts, so a change made mid-turn applies the threshold at that
  turn's end and clearing from the next turn. Risk accepted: with compaction off, requests fail
  at the model's window until Clear; with clearing on, the model may re-fetch a result it lost;
  and no proof has sent `context_management` to the real API — every live and stand-in run so
  far configured clearing off (`assistant_helper_proof.py`, `spend_proof.py`, the spike) and the
  unchanged helper builds the request, so a capped live clearing proof is owed, and the owner
  decides its spend.
  **Amended by NM-6** (rename R0): `ReelcutAssistantAutoCompact` is now
  `FrameJobAssistantAutoCompact`; `ReelcutAssistantAutoCompactTokens` is now
  `FrameJobAssistantAutoCompactTokens`; `ReelcutAssistantClearToolResults` is now
  `FrameJobAssistantClearToolResults`.
