# Spec §11 — decisions: Pricing and spend (road map 13)

Part of spec §11, *Decisions made — do not re-litigate*. The index of every decision is
[`README.md`](README.md).

The road map that made these is closed: its condensed record is `designs/adr/roadmap-13-pricing.md`,
and the original, `archive/roadmap-13.md`, words them in §3 and holds what was measured in §1
and §5.

- **P-1 — Prices come from LiteLLM's table.** A committed snapshot
  (`agent/prices/anthropic.json`) is refreshed daily at runtime and by `make prices`. Never
  hand-kept, except AssemblyAI's Universal-3.5 Pro rate, which no online source carries
  (`AssemblyAIRates`). Anthropic's page is the cross-check. `@pydantic/genai-prices` was rejected
  because it lacks the models Frame Job uses (road map 13 §1); the npm repackagings of LiteLLM add a
  lag and a dependency for four multiplications. Risk accepted: LiteLLM is a community table, and
  a wrong row is caught only by the cross-check, which compares the models Frame Job uses.
- **P-2 — A call is priced from the response's own `usage` and `model`, per token class, at that
  model's rates, in the helper — per `usage.iterations` entry when present, each at its own
  model, because the top-level counts describe only the attempt that returned the message and
  exclude compaction** (refusals-and-fallback.md, "Billing and rate limits"; the SDK's
  `BetaUsage.iterations` doc). Unknown models price as `unknown`, never $0; so does usage the
  table cannot price (a fast, priority/batch or US-only request, a malformed count, a class
  whose rate the row lacks). Risk accepted: a declined
  attempt in an unbilled refusal category is priced (an over-count); fast, priority/batch and
  US-only answer `unknown`.
- **P-3 — Budgets are dollars per calendar month per service** ($25 Anthropic, $5 AssemblyAI).
  They are enforced by the proofs before each request, at the worst case. Tokens are recorded for
  diagnosis and are never the budget. The budgets are the owner's numbers, committed; an agent
  never raises them.
- **P-4 — Spend shown in the app is Frame Job's own**, from its ledger, and says so. The Anthropic
  Console is the truth for the account.
- **P-5 — The spend ledger and the price cache are the person's, and a proof never touches them.**
  Both live in the spend folder, `~/Library/Application Support/Frame Job/` (`spend.jsonl`, one JSON
  line per priced response; `anthropic-prices.json`, the helper's daily copy of LiteLLM's table).
  `-RCSpendFolder <path>` replaces the folder, read from the argument domain alone (R6-9 (c)). With
  `RC_ASSISTANT_BASE_URL` set and no `-RCSpendFolder` there is NO spend folder: no ledger line is
  written, no cache is kept, and the helper prices from its bundled table and says so. The refresh
  fetches LiteLLM's raw `main` file; `-RCPriceFeed <url>` (argument domain) replaces it, and with
  the base URL set the cache is handed to the helper only together with `-RCPriceFeed`, so a proof
  never reaches LiteLLM. The helper refuses a feed that is neither https nor http to 127.0.0.1,
  localhost or ::1. A turn is priced with the prices in force at its `turn_started`; a refresh that
  settles mid-turn applies from the next turn. Risk accepted: two sessions opened at once may both
  fetch.
  **Amended by NM-4** (rename R0): the spend folder `~/Library/Application Support/Reelcut/` is now
  `~/Library/Application Support/Frame Job/`.
- **P-6 — The proofs' ledger is `~/Library/Application Support/Frame Job Proofs/spend.jsonl`, and
  every paid proof request is held to the month's budget in it before it is sent.** It is outside
  the repo, so it survives `rm -rf tools/proof/work` and a fresh clone and is shared by every
  worktree, and outside P-5's spend folder, which is the person's. `tools/proof/budget.py` is its
  only writer: one JSON line per event (`reserve`, `settle`, `refused`; `format` 1, `at` in UTC,
  `service`, `kind`, `id`), appended in one write to a file created 0600 in a folder created 0700,
  never a key, a header, a body or a text. The month is the UTC calendar month. A month's total for
  a service is a fold: a `reserve` made in the month counts its largest `settle`, or its `worst`
  while it has none; a `settle` with no `reserve` counts its own dollars in its own month; a
  `refused` counts nothing. The read, the fold and the append happen under one exclusive `flock` on
  the file, and a request is refused (`budget: …`) when the month's total plus its worst case would
  pass P-3's budget. It fails closed: a line that does not parse, or a ledger that cannot be read or
  written, refuses every paid request until a person repairs it. The worst case is the dearest the
  request can bill: for Anthropic, the relay's measure of the body and `max_tokens` at each token
  class's dearest rate over every row and `above_200k` tier of the price table; for AssemblyAI, the
  planned seconds at `AssemblyAIRates`' two rates added (speakers included). A reply is settled at
  the table's price; usage the table cannot price (an unknown model, a mode it has no rate for)
  settles at those dearest rates, and a reply whose usage cannot be read settles at its
  reservation. Only a keyed live run writes this ledger: rehearsals and verifications use scratch
  ledgers of their own. The budgets are constants in `budget.py`, pinned by `budget_proof.py`.
  Risk accepted: fast, priority and US-only usage is counted at the dearest standard rates (the
  helper requests none of them); a torn or hand-broken line stops every paid proof until a person
  repairs it. A keyed run of either road map 6 or 8 spike (`cloud_spike/`, `words_spike/`) reserves
  here too, through `cloud_live_ledger.spike_ledger`, beside its own $2.00 ledger (#163).
  **Amended by NM-4 and NM-7** (rename R0):
  `~/Library/Application Support/Reelcut Proofs/spend.jsonl` is now
  `~/Library/Application Support/Frame Job Proofs/spend.jsonl`; while
  `~/Library/Application Support/Reelcut Proofs/` exists, `budget.py` refuses every paid request in
  a sentence naming the guarded `mv` to the new name, and it refuses before it creates or writes
  anything under `Frame Job Proofs/` (no folder, no ledger, no `refused` event), so the month's
  total is never restarted at $0 and the owner's `mv` never nests.
  **Amended by NM-15** (#288): the owner moved the old proofs' ledger folder on 2026-10-13
  (#287), so the refusal while it exists is removed: `budget.py` holds every paid request to
  `~/Library/Application Support/Frame Job Proofs/spend.jsonl` alone, and nothing reads the old
  folder.
- **P-7 — The app shows two figures: what the current conversation has cost, on the Assistant
  tab, and what the UTC calendar month has cost, in Settings ▸ Assistant; both say they are
  Frame Job's own estimate (P-4).** The conversation figure is the transcript's sum of the `cost`
  events since its last Clear or ended conversation (a key or model change): kept in memory, it
  carries across a helper restart and is shown with no spend folder. The month figure is a fold of
  the spend folder's `spend.jsonl` over the **UTC** calendar month, because the ledger's `time` is
  UTC and P-6's budget month is UTC, so the app and the proofs count one month; its title says
  "(UTC)". The ledger is read only when Settings shows and after each line recorded while it is
  visible, and a read after a recorded line keeps the figure shown until its fold answers, so the
  window does not jump twice per response. An absent ledger answers at once on main; a present one
  is folded on one serial queue and only the latest read is shown. A line that could not be priced
  is counted and said, never added as $0 (P-2); a line that cannot be read is counted and said; a
  launch with no spend folder (P-5) says it keeps no ledger. Risk accepted: near the turn of a
  month the UTC month differs from the person's local calendar month by up to a day.
  **Amended by NM-5** (rename R0): "Reelcut's own estimate" is now "Frame Job's own estimate"
  (Settings' month note, "Frame Job's own estimate at LiteLLM prices, from its spend ledger.").
- **P-8 — A response cut short is priced once, from what its stream had reported, and marked
  partial.** The helper holds the SDK's accumulating snapshot of the response in flight
  (`message_start`'s counts and model, and each `message_delta`'s counts) until `finalMessage`
  resolves. A turn that throws — Stop, a network error, an API error mid-stream — with one held
  emits one `cost` with `partial: true`, at the turn's prices, before any `error`; a request that
  failed before `message_start` emits none. A response is never priced both complete and partial.
  The ledger line gains `"partial": true`; the turn line and the tab's Spend figure read "at
  least"; Settings' month fold sums a partial line's dollars like any priced line, unflagged.
  Where the tab's full figure does not fit its row, it reads "≥" for "at least" and "<" for
  "under", still ending "· Frame Job's estimate" (issue batch B47, #203). Before this, a response
  cut short was not priced at all (#162). Risk accepted: the figure is a lower bound — the API
  sends its one `message_delta` after the last content block, so a response cut short mid-stream
  is priced from `message_start`'s counts, its input and cache tokens, and in practice none of its
  streamed output; how the API bills an aborted stream is manual check AS-6's; the month line does
  not say that a line was partial.
  **Amended by NM-5** (rename R0): "· Reelcut's estimate" is now "· Frame Job's estimate".

content.content:
# Spec §11 — decisions: Cut by transcript (road map "cut-by-transcript")

Part of spec §11, *Decisions made — do not re-litigate*. The index of every decision is
[`README.md`](README.md).

The road map that made these is closed: its condensed record is `designs/adr/cut-by-transcript.md`,
and the original, `archive/cut-by-transcript.md`, holds each phase's record (CT-0 the road map,
these decisions and the filler spike; CT-1 fillers on the cloud request; CT-2 `detect_fillers`
and the cut; CT-3 Clip ▸ Remove Filler Words…; CT-4 `get_transcript` and false starts; CT-5 the
close). TR-1…TR-6 were recorded in CT-0, before any product code, from the owner's decisions of
2026-09-30 on issue #92 (its comment of that day, quoted verbatim in the road map's "The owner's
choices"), which the owner took up on 2026-10-22 ("#92 Cut by transcript"). TR-7, the on-device
filler source, was recorded on 2026-10-22 after the filler spike ran on the owner's own scripted
sample, before CT-2.
CT-1…CT-4 each record their numbers as a new entry (TR-8 on) or as Amended-by lines before their
code; TR-8 was recorded in CT-1, TR-9 in CT-2, TR-10 in CT-3 and TR-11 in CT-4, each before its
code. TR-12 was recorded in the #92 residue batch (#333), before its code. TR-13 was recorded in the #92
residue batch (#331), before its code.
TR-14 was recorded in the #92 residue batch (#332), before its code.

**Stands, and nothing here re-litigates it:** R6-3 (one upload per media, every clip derived from
it, the words cached verbatim); R6-10 (`MediaTranscript.words(for:in:)` maps a media's words onto
a clip); AI-7 (the cloud `transcribe` stays withheld from the assistant; TR-10 adds a row); W-8
(the on-device engine's asset download is a person's act, never a tool's); the silence road map's
32 ms grid (Silero VAD's own grid, inward; `silence.md`). R6-15 and AI-6 are amended here, by TR-1
and TR-5; W-9 is amended by TR-5 through AI-6; AI-7 is amended by TR-10; AI-16 is amended by
TR-11.

- **TR-1 — Fillers come from AssemblyAI's `disfluencies: true`, sent on every cloud request from
  CT-1 on, and the transcript marker records it.** The owner's decision 1 (#92, 2026-09-30).
  - **The request:** `TranscriptOptions` and `TranscriptRequest` (`AssemblyAITranscript.swift`)
    gain `disfluencies`, true on every request CT-1 and later sends; `TranscriptStamp` records it,
    so a marker identifies the request it was made with, as R6-15 says a marker must. This
    amends R6-15.
  - **Captions look unchanged:** the caption producers (`CaptionPages.normalize`/`cues`,
    `CaptionLayout.place`) never see a filler: `MediaTranscript.words(for:in:)`'s caption callers
    drop them, against one filler vocabulary, so a caption made from a disfluent transcript is
    byte-identical to one made from the same words without the option.
  - **Why:** AssemblyAI reports "um" and "uh" only when asked, and a transcript-level cut needs
    them timed. Road map 6 refused the option because "um" is not a caption
    (`archive/roadmap-6.md` l.152); that refusal is superseded here, and the filter keeps the
    reason it was made.
  - Risk accepted: every cloud transcript from CT-1 on carries words no caption shows, and the
    vocabulary that drops them must match AssemblyAI's spelling, which CT-1 pins against its
    documentation and `assemblyai_fake.py`.
- **TR-2 — A transcript cached before CT-1 stays current for captions; it is re-transcribed only
  when the person asks for filler removal on that media, after the estimate line has shown the
  cost.** The owner's decision 1, its first sub-point.
  - **The marker rule:** a caption run takes a current marker whatever its `disfluencies` value
    (an old marker, with no key, reads as false); a filler run needs a marker with
    `disfluencies` true. Nothing re-transcribes on its own.
  - **The ask:** the Remove Filler Words sheet (CT-3) shows media with no disfluent transcript
    with its `CloudEstimate` line and a Transcribe button; the re-transcribe is that person's
    press, one media at a time as the sheet lists them.
  - Risk accepted: a project transcribed before CT-1 needs a second paid transcription before its
    fillers can be cut.
- **TR-3 — Two paths, split by who judges: fillers are deterministic, and false starts are a
  judgement of meaning.** The owner's decision 2.
  - A filler is a word in a closed vocabulary, found by its spelling and cut on its own timing:
    no judgement of meaning, so a pipeline may do it (TR-4).
  - A false start ("I was — we were going") is found only by reading what was meant, so no
    pipeline does it (W-9, AI-6); the assistant may, when the person asks (TR-5).
  - Risk accepted: a filler the vocabulary does not spell, or one the engine did not report, is
    not offered; a false start is never offered without a conversation.
- **TR-4 — Remove Filler Words… is shaped like Remove Silences: a sheet, a candidate wash on the
  timeline, one `ripple_delete_ranges` undo step, and its own read-half MCP tool,
  `detect_fillers`.** The owner's decision 2, its first sub-point.
  - **The pieces:** `detect_fillers` answers the ranges and cuts nothing, as `detect_silence`
    does (`AgentServer+Silence.swift`); the cut is the existing `ripple_delete_ranges`
    (`core/src/edit.rs`), so the menu command and an agent make the same single undo step. The
    sheet (`FillerSheetController.swift`, CT-3) is shaped like `SilenceSheetController`, and its
    wash comes from `TimelineView+Candidates.swift`.
  - **No new op and no format change:** a filler range is a range like a silence's; nothing new
    is persisted in the project.
  - **The edges:** on the Silero VAD's 32 ms grid (`MediaSpeech`, `SileroVAD.chunkSamples`),
    frame-snapped as `SilenceDetector` snaps; the exact rule is a TR entry CT-2 records before
    its code. That is #92's done-when: a known filler cut out of a fixture, its ranges read back
    through `get_project`, its edges on the grid.
  - Risk accepted: the cut is only as tight as the transcript's word timings and the grid allow.
- **TR-5 — False starts go to the assistant under AI-6, which this amends: the assistant may
  choose words to cut when the person asks, reading them through a new app-state tool,
  `get_transcript`.** The owner's decision 2, its second sub-point.
  - **The tool:** `get_transcript` answers a clip's words in timeline times, fillers flagged. It
    reads the current cloud cache when there is one, else runs the on-device engine over the
    clip's window, and it never makes a network call, so AI-7 still withholds the cloud
    `transcribe` and nothing about it changes.
  - **The rule:** no PIPELINE picks words by meaning (W-9, AI-6, unchanged). The assistant chooses
    words to cut only because the person asked in the conversation; it proposes, then makes
    ordinary undoable cuts (`ripple_delete_ranges`), each an undo step like any other edit.
  - Risk accepted: the assistant's choice of a false start can be wrong; the person sees the
    proposal first and undo takes back what it cut.
- **TR-6 — The working arrangement: the `transcript-cut` worktree, each phase gated, committed and
  merged into main alone.** The owner's ask of 2026-10-22.
  - The worktree is `~/devel/framejob-tcut` on branch `transcript-cut`, from `c3731fa`; each
    phase passes `make gate`, is committed and is merged into main alone, with main's next
    numbers if main moved.
  - Fixtures are synthetic (`say`) and AssemblyAI is `assemblyai_fake.py`; a paid call runs only
    behind its explicit flags and the month's budget (P-3, P-6), and only when a change is likely
    to break what it tests. The owner's `tools/proof/media/owner-sync*` and `filler-sample/` are
    read in place and never committed or copied out.
  - Agents edit no `CLAUDE.md`; each phase's handback lists the edits owed.
  - Risk accepted: until the owner's scripted sample (o2) is recorded, no owner recording holds
    a known filler; a real recording's filler CUT stays a person's check.
- **TR-7 — Filler removal is cloud-only: the on-device engine is not a filler source.** Recorded
  2026-10-22, before CT-2, by the owner ("Cloud-only (Recommended)") after the filler spike's run
  on the owner's scripted sample (`tools/proof/filler_spike/`, `answers.json`).
  - **Measured** (macOS 26.5.1, en-US, on-device): on the owner reading the eight-filler script
    (o2, 29.4 s), the engine recognised 98.3 % of the script's other words and kept **1 of 8**
    fillers (the first "um"; the other two um, all three uh and both er dropped). On `say`
    speech it kept 6 of 8 (f1) and 7 of 8 (f2); the no-filler control kept 0. The spike's
    mechanical verdict is `reports-real` (any kept filler counts); one in eight is not a source.
  - **So:** `detect_fillers` and Remove Filler Words… read fillers only from a transcript whose
    marker serves `.fillers` (TR-2); for media with none, the sheet says filler removal needs a
    cloud transcript and offers the estimated re-transcribe (TR-2, TR-4). On-device captions are
    unchanged and filter nothing.
  - Risk accepted: a person with no AssemblyAI key has no filler removal. One speaker, one
    script, one Mac; a later engine that keeps fillers would be a new decision.
- **TR-8 — The caption filler vocabulary is: um, uh, hmm, mhm, uh-huh, ah, huh, hm, m, er, erm.**
  Recorded in CT-1, before its code (`FillerWords.assemblyAI`, `FillerWords.swift`).
  - **The sources, as read on 2026-10-22:** AssemblyAI's Universal-2 "Filler words" page
    (https://www.assemblyai.com/docs/filler-words, read through a search summary) lists the first
    nine. The older core-transcription page lists five of them (um, uh, hmm, mhm, uh huh). The
    current page (https://www.assemblyai.com/docs/pre-recorded-audio/filler-words) gives only "uh"
    and "um" as examples, and says `disfluencies` applies to Universal-3.5 Pro and Universal-2.
    AssemblyAI's Universal-3 Pro prompting material names er, erm, ah, hmm and mhm as fillers.
  - **No published list for the first model:** Universal-3.5 Pro, the first model the app
    requests, has no published list, so the nine words are documented for Universal-2 only, and
    no published list guarantees that captions equal those made before CT-1.
    `cloud_captions_live.py` row 22 records what the real service returns.
  - **The match:** a word is a filler when its text, lowercased, with leading and trailing
    punctuation and whitespace trimmed, is in the list. "uh huh" is matched by its two halves,
    and `uh-huh` as one token. Captions drop exactly these. The cache keeps every served word
    verbatim (R6-3). Another source's fillers (TR-7) are added by that source's own entry.
  - **Why:** these are the tokens AssemblyAI itself names as fillers for the models the app
    requests.
  - Risk accepted: a real "ah" or "er", or the letter "M", is dropped from captions. A filler the
    service returns outside this list is captioned until a later decision adds it.
- **TR-9 — Filler cut edges are the transcript's filler runs, widened to the Silero 32 ms grid
  within the words beside them, then snapped inward to the frame grid.** Recorded in CT-2,
  before its code (`FillerDetector.swift`, `detect_fillers`).

before its code (`FillerDetector.swift`, `detect_fillers`).
  - **The words:** a clip's words are its media's cached words that belong to it by R6-10 (start
    in `[in, in + content_length)`), sorted by `(start, end)`, milliseconds to ticks through
    `MediaTranscript.sourceTicks` (the end uses `max(start, end)`). A **run** is a maximal
    sequence of consecutive `FillerWords.isFiller` words in that order; its source span is
    `[first.start, max end)`.
  - **The neighbours:** `previousEnd` is the larger of `in` and the latest end of every
    non-filler word sorted before the run; `nextStart` is the smaller of `in + content_length`
    and the earliest start of every non-filler word sorted after it.
  - **The grid:** G = `MediaSpeech.chunkTicks` (512 samples at 16 kHz, absolute source time from
    0, the speech cache's own index). `start = max(floor(run.start / G)·G,
    ceil(previousEnd / G)·G)` and `end = min(ceil(run.end / G)·G, floor(nextStart / G)·G)`:
    outward to the grid so the whole filler goes, never into a neighbouring word. `end ≤ start`
    drops the run (too short).
  - **The frame grid:** each edge maps to project time through `MediaTranscript.project` (R6-10's
    door), then `SilenceDetector.snapUpToFrame` (start) and `snapDownToFrame` (end), inward as
    Remove Silences snaps; `end ≤ start` drops it (too short).
  - **A locked track:** a clip on a locked track gives no candidates, because
    `ripple_delete_ranges` neither splits nor shifts a locked track (`core/src/edit_time.rs`), so
    the filler would stay and everything else would slide. A track the snapshot cannot find
    counts as unlocked, as the nest walls do.
  - **What drops a candidate, whole:** a project span that overlaps (half-open, more than 0
    ticks) a non-filler word (`MediaTranscript.words(for:in:)`) of any OTHER clip on an unlocked
    track whose media's transcript serves `.captions` — in scope or not, because the ripple cuts
    every unlocked track; one that crosses a nest clip; one that crosses a transition wall
    (`SilenceDetector.overlapWalls`). Checked in that order, and dropped whole, never trimmed, so
    every kept edge is a grid edge. Kept spans are merged where they overlap or touch.
  - **Nothing else:** no probability is read, no padding or threshold applies; a reversed clip
    and a clip `Transcriber.jobs` refuses have no words.
  - Risk accepted: the cut is only as tight as the words' timings; an inward frame snap can leave
    up to a frame of a filler; speech on an unlocked track whose media has no transcript is not
    protected.
- **TR-10 — Clip ▸ Remove Filler Words… is a sheet with no tuning controls over `detect_fillers`'
  answer, and its Transcribe button re-transcribes one media with that media's previous request
  plus fillers; its mirror, `transcribe_for_fillers`, is always withheld from the assistant
  (amends AI-7).** Recorded in CT-3, before its code (`FillerSheetController.swift`,
  `FillerSheetController+Transcribe.swift`, `FillerTranscription.swift`,
  `AgentServer+Fillers.swift`).
  - **The sheet:** no controls to tune, because TR-9 has no threshold. Its scope is
    `detect_fillers`' opening rule (`FillerDetector.read(from:clips: nil)`: the selection when it
    holds a clip with speech from a media file, else every clip), and its note says when the
    scope is the selection. Remove sends ONE `ripple_delete_ranges` of the sheet's spans, undo
    name "Remove Filler Words". The wash is `TimelineView.candidateSpans`, set by the sheet and
    cleared in its `viewDidDisappear`. The menu item comes right after Remove Silences…, has no
    key equivalent (Remove Silences…' reason) and is enabled by
    `Transcriber.hasTranscribableClip`.
  - **The re-transcribe:** one media per press. It keeps that media's previous request — the
    marker's language, speaker labels and vocabulary — with the shipped models,
    `disfluencies: true` and `refresh: true`; with no earlier marker it detects the language,
    with no speakers and no vocabulary. The row's estimate is `CloudEstimate.describe` of that
    same request. Before any Transcribe button can be enabled the sheet says where the audio
    goes, in which region, and that it is deleted once read back (R6-2, kept): Generate
    Captions…' AssemblyAI sentence with "Transcribe" for "Generate". Remove is disabled while a
    run is going, so Return can neither cut nor cancel a paid upload mid-run. No caption is
    placed and no undo step is made: the run only writes the media's transcript cache.
  - **The mirror:** `transcribe_for_fillers {media}`, an app-state tool that runs off the main
    thread with the button's request and answers `ready` (whether the media now has a filler
    transcript) with `transcribe`'s cloud fields; a media already ready makes no request. It is
    always withheld from the assistant, with R6-2's reason pointing at the sheet, which amends
    AI-7.
  - Risk accepted: a request that had speaker labels is billed again with the speakers
    surcharge, and its vocabulary carries over unseen; the person sees the price first.
- **TR-11 — `get_transcript {clip, language?}` answers one clip's words in timeline ticks with
  fillers flagged, from the media's cached transcript or else this Mac's recogniser, never the
  network; the run is off main and the assistant's Stop reaches it (amends AI-16); the prompt
  teaches the false-start path.** Recorded in CT-4, before its code (`TranscriptReader.swift`,
  `AgentServer+Transcript.swift`, `AssistantPrompt.swift`).
  - **The source:** the media's cached transcript when its marker serves `.captions` for the file
    as it is now (`FillerDetector.transcriptFile(for:url:in:use: .captions)`, TR-2's one rule, no
    new marker rule), and only when the document has a cache directory; else the on-device engine
    over the clip's own source window (`Transcriber().extractAudio`, then
    `SpeechEngine.transcribe`, the temporary WAV removed on every exit). Never the network (TR-5),
    and no cache is written: an on-device run is repeated on every call.
  - **The words:** a cached transcript's through R6-10's mapping (`MediaTranscript.words(for:in:)`),
    an on-device run's through `Transcriber.project`, a run whose mapped start is at or past the
    clip's end dropped. Either list is sorted by start, then end, then its order in the source.
    `filler` is TR-8's rule (`FillerWords.isFiller`) for either engine, and nothing is filtered
    out. `speaker` only where the cached word has one. `fillers_reported` is whether the
    transcript was asked for fillers (`FillerDetector.fillersFile` answers): false for every
    on-device run and for a cached transcript made without `disfluencies`.
  - **The refusals, in order:** the clip (`clipArg`'s own sentences); a clip `Transcriber.jobs`
    refuses, "Clip <id> has no words to read: <reason>."; the language's spelling (`transcribe`'s
    `checkSpelling`); then, with no cached transcript only, the installed model (`transcribe`'s
    `transcriptionLanguage`) and the recogniser's own `TranscribeError` sentence. `language`
    applies to the recogniser only. The clip, the jobs and the cache are read in one main-thread
    hop.
  - **The answer:** `ok`, `clip`, `media`, `engine` (`assemblyai` or `apple`), `language` (the
    cached header's `language_code` or the recogniser's identifier; omitted when nil),
    `fillers_reported`, `count`, `words` (`text`, `start`, `end`, `filler`, and `speaker` when
    known), `note` when there is something to say ("No words were heard in clip <id>." for an
    empty list; "These words were not transcribed with filler words, so a filler missing here
    may still be in the audio." when `fillers_reported` is false), and `project`. Nothing is
    edited and no undo step is made.
  - **Off main, and Stop (amends AI-16):** the tool runs on the server thread
    (`AgentServer.offMainTools`). Its first line reads `AgentLane.shared.callCancel`, and the
    on-device run's `Transcriber.CancelToken` is linked to it exactly as `transcribe` links its
    own (`stop?.onCancel { token.cancel() }`), so the assistant's Stop ends the run and the model
    gets "The transcription was cancelled.".
  - **No AI-7 row:** it writes nothing, uploads nothing and spends nothing, so the assistant may
    call it without asking.
  - **The prompt:** the assistant's system text gains this paragraph, after the Captions and
    Graphics paragraph, verbatim: "Cutting words: `detect_fillers` answers the filler words (um,
    uh) as ranges for `ripple_delete_ranges`. A false start, words the speaker abandoned or said
    again, is a judgement of meaning, so cut one only when the person asks: read the clip's words
    and their times with `get_transcript`, say which words you will cut, then cut them in one
    `ripple_delete_ranges` call, each range from the first cut word's start to the last cut
    word's end." Its search guide's captions row reads "captions: import, transcribe speech, read
    a clip's timed words, export a caption file" and gains `get_transcript` after `transcribe`.
  - Risk accepted: a long clip's answer is large (every word, no window; a `from`/`to` window is
    CT-5's residue to file), and an on-device answer is recognised again on every call.
  - **Amended 2026-10-23, by TR-13:** the missing window is `get_transcript`'s `from`/`to`
    (#331); a call without them answers exactly as above.
  - **Amended 2026-10-23, by TR-14:** an on-device run's words are now cached per media and
    language (#332), so "The source"'s "no cache is written: an on-device run is repeated on every
    call" no longer holds, and neither does the risk bullet's "an on-device answer is recognised
    again on every call": a call whose span is inside a stored run answers from it. "The words"'
    on-device mapping is TR-14's: stored media source ticks, kept by R6-10's half-open source-window
    test and mapped by `MediaTranscript.project`, replacing `Transcriber.project` and the
    mapped-start drop test.
- **TR-12 — An agent's `ripple_delete_ranges` names its undo step "Ripple Delete", whatever it
  cuts; the tool takes no name.** Recorded in the #92 residue batch (#333), before its code
  (`AgentServer+Clips.swift`).
  - **The name:** it is the step name of Edit ▸ Ripple Delete (⌘⌫) and of the `ripple_delete` and
    `ripple_delete_range` tools: what the op does, which is true of silences, fillers (TR-4), a
    false start (TR-11) or a caller's own ranges. Until now the tool used "Remove Silences", the
    sheet's name, so Edit ▸ Undo misnamed every cut that was not a silence.
  - **The menus keep theirs:** Clip ▸ Remove Silences… names its step "Remove Silences" and
    Clip ▸ Remove Filler Words… "Remove Filler Words" (TR-10). TR-4's "the same single undo step"
    stands: it means one step, not one name.
  - **No caller-passed name:** every op tool's step name is fixed by the tool. A name argument
    would be a tool-only argument (an `AgentCatalog+Declarations.swift` row, §6, the gate), free
    text an agent writes into Edit ▸ Undo, and one more lesson for the assistant's prompt.
  - **Proof:** `phase3_proof.py` C3 reads "Ripple Delete" after a silence cut, and
    `fillers_proof.py` M2 reads it after a filler cut.
  - Risk accepted: after an agent's silence cut, Edit ▸ Undo reads "Undo Ripple Delete", not the
    sheet's "Undo Remove Silences".
- **TR-13 — `get_transcript {clip, language?, from?, to?}` answers only the words that overlap
  the timeline window [from, to), clamped to the clip; an on-device run hears only that window
  and 2 s of source either side.** Recorded in the #92 residue batch (#331), before its code
  (`TranscriptReader.swift`, `AgentServer+Transcript.swift`, `AgentCatalog+Captions.swift`).
  - **The arguments:** `from` and `to` are optional timeline ticks (600000 per second), read by
    `optionalTimeArg` and so snapped to the frame grid like every tick a tool takes. Either may be
    given alone: a missing `from` is the clip's start, a missing `to` its end. With neither the
    call is TR-11's, unchanged.
  - **The clamp:** the window is [max(from, clip start), min(to, clip end)), so a window wider
    than the clip answers the whole clip's words.
  - **Overlap and edges:** a word belongs to the window when it starts before `to` and ends after
    `from` (a word with no length, when `from` ≤ its start < `to`). A word across either edge is
    answered whole, with its own times, never cut at the edge; the order is TR-11's.
  - **The refusals, in TR-11's order:** the clip; the jobs refusal; a `from` or `to` that is not
    a time (`optionalTimeArg`'s own sentence, "from must be a time in ticks (600000 per
    second)."); an empty window, both bounds given and `to` not after `from` ("to must be after
    from: the window from <from> to <to> ticks (both snapped to frames) is empty."); a window
    outside the clip, empty once clamped ("The window <bounds> is outside clip <id>, which plays
    from <start> to <end> ticks.", `<bounds>` the bounds the call gave, snapped: "from F to T",
    "from F" or "to T"); then the language's spelling, the installed model and the recogniser.
    The window is read in the same main-thread hop as the clip, the jobs and the cache.
  - **The answer:** a call that gave `from` or `to` gains `from` and `to`, the window as applied
    (snapped and clamped); `count` counts the words in the window, and an empty list's note is
    "No words were heard in clip <id> between <from> and <to> ticks.". Every other key and note
    is TR-11's.
  - **The on-device run narrowed:** the recogniser hears the window plus 2 s of SOURCE on each
    side, clamped to the clip (`TranscriptReader.recognitionJob`: a sub-job whose start, duration
    and `in` point are the padded window's, so `Transcriber.project`'s premise, that the extract
    begins at the job's `in`, still holds). The pad means a word across an edge is heard whole;
    words heard in the pad that do not reach the window are dropped by the overlap rule.
  - **One filter for both engines (#332):** the window is a filter on MAPPED words
    (`TranscriptReader.overlapping`), applied to the cached path's words and the on-device
    path's alike; `recognitionJob` is only the on-device run's input. So a later per-media,
    per-language cache of on-device words (#332) can recognise wider than the window and answer
    through the same filter.
    **Amended 2026-10-23, by TR-14:** that cache is built (#332); a stored run wider than the
    window answers through this filter.
  - Risk accepted: a windowed on-device answer can differ from the whole clip's words at the
    same times, because the recogniser hears less context. The cached path's words in a window
    are identical to the whole clip's in that window.
- **TR-14 — `get_transcript` caches what this Mac's recogniser heard, per media and language,
  keyed by the file's identity; a later call whose span is inside a stored run answers from it
  without recognising again. The cache is `get_transcript`'s alone.** Recorded in the #92 residue
  batch (#332), before its code (`DeviceTranscriptCache.swift`, `TranscriptReader.swift`,
  `AgentServer+Transcript.swift`, `AgentCatalog+Captions.swift`).
  - **What and where:** `cache/device-transcripts/<media id>-<language identifier>.json`, one JSON
    file per (media, language) holding the whole cached state, written with sorted keys; it never
    shares `cache/transcripts/` with AssemblyAI's files. It follows the cache folder's rules:
    regenerable; carried by every save, since `cache/` travels whole; in an untitled document's
    temporary cache until its first save; written whole and atomic through
    `MediaImporter.CacheLedger.shared.publish(in:for: nil)`, so it never lands mid-save. A file
    that is missing, unreadable or of another shape reads as absent. A document with no cache
    directory, a media the snapshot lacks, or a file that cannot be stat'ed (nil `CacheStamp`)
    reads nothing and writes nothing, and runs as TR-11 did. Nothing is held in memory between
    calls. There is no size cap: a file holds only what was heard.
  - **The key:** the stamp is R6-15's four-field `TranscriptSourceStamp` (the path is not in it,
    for `CacheStamp`'s reason), the resolved BCP-47 language, the OS version string (the
    recogniser ships with the OS), and `version` 1. A file whose stamp is not equal is a miss, and
    the next store replaces it whole. Model availability: `transcriptionLanguage` still runs first
    on every call, so a language whose model is gone is refused as before; a hit skips
    `recognize`'s own model questions. Risk accepted: a model asset updated without an OS update
    is not seen.
  - **The window rule:** a call needs the source span its run would hear: the clip's window, or,
    with `from`/`to`, `recognitionJob`'s padded window. A hit is the first stored run, in file
    order, whose span contains that span. A miss runs exactly that span, so the first windowed
    call costs what TR-13 costs: the window plus 2 s of source each side. The store then drops
    every stored run the new one contains. There is no gap-filling and no merging of words across
    runs. So a whole-clip call after windowed ones runs once, and every window inside it hits
    after that. Risk accepted: the same windowed call can answer differently before and after a
    wider run is stored (TR-13's context risk).
  - **The mapping (replaces TR-11's `Transcriber.project` mapping):** a run's seconds are stored
    as `run.sourceIn + round(clamp(t × 600000, 0, run.sourceLength))` media source ticks, and a
    non-finite time is dropped. A clip takes a stored word when its source start is in the clip's
    `[sourceIn, sourceIn + sourceLength)` (R6-10's half-open test). Its start and its end, read as
    `max(start, end)`, map through `MediaTranscript.project(_:in:)`. Then come TR-11's sort,
    TR-8's flag and TR-13's overlap filter. The stored runs are per media, so another clip, speed
    or window over the same file reuses them.
  - **Whose cache:** only `get_transcript` reads it. It is never read by captions (on-device or
    cloud), Remove Filler Words, `detect_fillers` or `transcribe_for_fillers` (TR-7: fillers are
    cloud-only); `TranscriptReader.cached`, `FillerDetector.transcriptFile` and `CloudEstimate`
    never read it. A cloud transcript that serves `.captions` still answers first.
    `fillers_reported` stays false for the on-device engine.
  - **Stop and failure:** Stop ends a run as before. Nothing is stored when a run throws (cancel
    or error), when the token was cancelled after the run returned, or when the file's stamp
    changed during the run.
  - **The answer and AI-7:** an engine `apple` answer gains `cached` (true when it came from a
    stored run); an `assemblyai` answer is unchanged. AI-7 still has no row: the tool writes only
    a regenerable cache, with no edit, no undo step, nothing dirtied and no network. Two calls at
    once may both run, and the last store wins.

# app/CLAUDE.md — Swift app rules

Applies to everything under `app/`. Build/verification commands and the FFI
lockstep are in the root `CLAUDE.md`; the full design is
`designs/spec/` (§3–4 the UI, §7.4–7.8 the platform side; its `README.md` is
the index). The
long form of each entry below — why each file is the shape it is, and the
traps its history turned up — is `designs/adr/app-file-history.md` (the
full history, every size toll and measurement, is archived; see its
"Original" line); this file is what governs a file now. Files
are listed by family; a file with a header comment of its own carries its
detail there.

## File map

**The core's edge.**
- `ReelCore.swift` — the **only** home for `rc_*` calls: `ReelProject`
  (handle + lazily decoded `ProjectSnapshot`; `json`, `snapshot` and
  `planJSON` are memoised PER HANDLE, so keep handles rather than minting
  them; so is `sourceMap(_:)`, `rc_project_source_map` decoded and checked
  once per handle and clip, SR-20), timecode, snapping (export presets/sizes/settings are
  `ExportValues.swift`'s, a pure move, HDR H-1), `ReelSpeed.limits` (the
  core's speed range and audio ceiling, typed as `SpeedLimits` in
  `CoreValues.swift` — no Swift file types a speed bound), `ReelColor` (`rc_normalise_color`, G-25), `ReelGraphicPackage` (`rc_graphic_package_write`, G-46; `read`, `rc_graphic_package_read`, G-47), `GraphicLibrary.usage()` (`rc_graphic_library_usage`) and
  `ReelContainer` (`rc_container_*`, a WebM/Matroska file's index,
  #216-R) and `ReelWebM` (`rc_webm_*`, the `av1_webm` writer, spec §11 CX-15) and `ReelHDR10` (`rc_hdr10_peak`, spec §11 HD-6; `av1Peak`,
  `rc_hdr10_av1_peak`, HD-18; `stillPeak`, `rc_hdr10_still_peak`, HD-20), and `GraphicLibrary.imageCache(limit:)`
  (`rc_graphic_image_cache`, G-39); `ReelCoreError`, `Fps.ffiPair` and `ReelTime`'s
  seconds conversions are `CoreValues.swift`'s (G6 phase 5's toll T2 and speed ramps SR4-0,
  pure moves); the typed patches are `TypedPatches.swift`'s (`VideoPatch`,
  `AudioPatch`, `ClipPatch`, the `ActionPatch` extension; a pure move, B73),
  `TextPatch` (with `case`, `words` and `word_style`) is `TextPatch.swift`'s,
  moved out so it could grow, and `ShapePatch` `ShapePatch.swift`'s (a pure
  move, the toll for `ReelColor`). `VideoPatch.color` is a sparse `ColorPatch`
  (`GradeProps.swift`, which holds `ColorAdjust` (moved out of
  `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, grading-2 G2-0) with its neutrality helpers, and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(tone:)`, and the wheels' `ColorWheel`, `ColorWheels`,
  `ColorWheelPatch`, `ColorWheelsPatch`, `ColorWheelKind` and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(wheels:)` (GR-11)); `VideoPatch.curves` is
  `CurveProps.swift`'s `ColorCurvesPatch`, beside `CurvePoint`,
  `CurveDomain`, `CurveChannel`, `CurveBlend` (a channel blended inside an
  action, spec §11 GR-34; `ColorCurves.blends`, never encoded), `ColorCurves` and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(curves:)` (GR-12, the hue curves GR-32; a
  pure move out of `GradeProps.swift`, grading-4 T4-0); `VideoPatch.qualifier` is
  `QualifierProps.swift`'s `ColorQualifierPatch`, beside `ColorQualifier` (its
  `blur`, `blursSelection` and `selectionSigma`, GR-35), `QualifierUniforms`
  (`blurred`, set only by `drawAdjustment`) and the pick's `QualifierSample`
  (GR-13), so a row writes
  only its own key to every selected clip. `word_style` has ONE
  app-side writer, `CaptionLayout.place` (W-10). `ReelAgentSocket` (road map
  14's MC2) wraps `rc_agent_socket_start` / `_release`: `start` throws the
  core's sentence, `release` is the quit's unlink-if-still-ours with no join.
  The `dictionary` extensions on the property types are
  `OpDictionaries.swift`'s (below).
  The graphics engine's wrappers are here too: `GraphicLibrary` (`addFont`,
  `addAsset`, `rasterize`, `families()`; frozen by its first compile,
  rasterize or `families()`) and
  `GraphicModule` (`compile`, `describeJSON`, `svg`; it holds its library
  strongly); their values `GraphicDiagnostic` (with `.error`, `.noModule`
  and `.of(_:)`, the one spelling of a diagnostic made from a message, a
  missing module or a thrown error), `GraphicFailure` (what a
  `diag_out` failure throws; `err_out` stays `ReelCoreError`) and
  `GraphicRaster` are `CoreValues.swift`'s, with `GraphicUsage`, the byte
  bridges `withByteBuffer` and `withMutableByteBuffer` (G-46's toll; never
  `UnsafeMutablePointer(mutating:)`), `SpeedLimits` (a pure move,
  clean-up batch 2), `ReelCoreError` and `Fps.ffiPair` (G6 phase 5's toll), and
  `CoreJSON` (`value`, `snapTicks`: `clipState`'s and `snapCandidates`' JSON
  halves, clean-up round 3's toll; `array`, `overrides`, C1's tolls; `ExportSize.list`,
  `ExportSettings.decoded`, `ReelAV1.Config.decoded`, `withNonNullBytes`, codec-export C5's
  toll), and C1's
  fix-pass moves: `ReelAV1.Config` / `.Color` (an extension of `ReelCore.swift`'s
  `ReelAV1`, whose `rc_av1_*` calls stay there), `GraphicDiagnostic.list(json:)`,
  `GraphicFailure.checkSides`, `SpeedLimits.decoded` and the free `withBytes`.
  `MediaDescriptor`, `MediaOriginal`, `mediaURL(for:)`, `originalURL(for:)`,
  `revealURL(for:)` (the original, else the copy), `isTrashed` and
  `bookmarkString(for:)` are `MediaDescriptor.swift`'s: a `media[]` element
  minus its id, and the media-file resolvers; they call no `rc_*`.
  It is also where the op table is read BACK: `ReelOp.coreNames()` over
  `rc_op_names`, and `ReelOp.coreSchemas()` over `rc_op_schemas` — every
  op's ARGUMENTS as JSON Schema, keyed by op name, which
  `AgentCatalog.opTool` prints for all sixty-four op tools.
  `deinit` frees the Rust allocation. It also holds **the one read of
  `rc_project_apply`'s TWO message channels**, in the header's own order — a
  sentence is a refusal, an error message is invalid input, neither written
  is an identity — answered as the `ReelEdit` below.
- `OpDictionaries.swift` — the `dictionary` extensions on the §5.2
  property types (`CropInsets` … `Gradient`), the model's own key names; a
  pure move out of `ReelCore.swift` (#190, issue batch B52b; road map 14's
  MC2 made the same move as `PropsDictionaries.swift`, and the merge kept
  main's file). With
  `ReelCore.swift` and `ReelOps.swift`, the only files that write an op
  argument. `putNullable` is the one writer of a three-state (`T??`)
  patch key: absent, an explicit null, or the value.
- `ReelOps.swift` — `OpArgs`, `ReelOp` and one typed factory per row of
  `core/src/edit.rs`'s op table, plus a RAW factory beside the typed one at
  each door that takes a CALLER's own object — ELEVEN of them (`setVideoRaw`,
  `setAudioRaw`, `setTextRaw`, `setShapeRaw`, `setClipRaw`,
  `setActionEndRaw`, `addTextClipRaw`, `addShapeClipRaw`, `setCanvasRaw`,
  `addBackgroundRaw`, `addZoomActionRaw`), which takes the
  caller's own object as `Any` — never `[String: Any]`, so a non-object is
  refused by the CORE in the words that name the group — and forwards it;
  there is no untyped op-JSON call site anywhere else. Where only ONE
  argument is the caller's (a colour, a region, a new clip's patch) the typed
  factory DELEGATES to the raw one, mapping its optional explicitly, because
  an `Optional<T>.none` widened to `Any?` is a non-nil `Any` wrapping a nil.
  The typed `setActionEnd` LIFTS every top-level null out of its patch into
  `off` (spec §11 CI-14: a typed `.some(nil)` is a switch turned OFF, kept
  at the end), and a null slot inside `audio.eq` into `audio.eq.<slot>`
  (AU-88); `setActionEndRaw`'s nulls stay removals, which is what
  `clearOps` and every agent call send, and it writes `off` only when non-empty and `schema` only when non-nil
  (the agent door fills it for a graphic end from the module's current
  revision, spec §11 G-34).
  `addZoomActionRaw`'s region is `Any` and not `Any?`: an absent key and an
  explicit null are opposite intentions there, and only the tool can tell
  them apart.
  `scope` is a member folded into `json`; `documentLevelNames` MIRRORS
  `scope.rs`'s `refused_inside` (eight names) so one edit can mix a
  document-level op with scoped ones. A table, with
  `edit.rs`'s size exemption.
- `ReelOpSchema.swift` — what an op TAKES, mirroring what
  `core/src/op_schema.rs` publishes: the `properties` and `required` of one
  op's arguments, which are the two things `AgentServer.tool` takes, and
  `table(from:)`, which reads `rc_op_schemas`' JSON into them (SR4-0's pure
  move out of `ReelCore.swift`, whose `coreSchemas()` keeps the call). Here
  rather than next door for `ReelEdit.swift`'s reason — it names no `rc_*`
  symbol — and `properties` stays `[String: Any]` because a Swift type per
  kind would be another spelling of the table.
- `ReelEdit.swift` — what an op ANSWERS, mirroring `core/src/outcome.rs`:
  `ReelEdit` (`.applied` / `.identity` / `.refused`), `ReelRefusal` (the op
  the core declined and the rule's own sentence, carried verbatim), and the
  fold that applies a LIST — which names no `rc_*` symbol, so it lives here
  and not next door. **Only `.applied` is an undo step**; the other two are
  both "the project did not change" and differ only in what a caller can
  SAY. `.project` is the spelling for a caller that treats a refusal as
  nothing happened (a probe, a live drag), and there is one on
  `ReelEdit?` too for the `try?` probes. In the fold **a refusal does not
  stop the list** — a later op still runs after one, exactly as after an
  identity — and the FIRST refusal is answered only when nothing applied.
- `ProjectSnapshot.swift` · `TextProps.swift` · `MotionProps.swift` ·
  `WordProps.swift` · `MediaSnapshot.swift` · `ActionSnapshot.swift` · `ShapeProps.swift` · `CompositionPlan.swift` · `GradeProps.swift` · `CurveProps.swift` · `AudioProps.swift` — the `Codable`, READ-ONLY mirror
  of spec §5.2 every view draws from. READ-ONLY means never written back as
  is: the stored properties are `var`, so a writer edits a COPY
  (`var s = current(); s.blur = v`) rather than rebuilding one through the
  defaulted memberwise initialiser, which silently drops a field it does not
  spell out; `MotionProps.with(_:)` is motion's per-slot copy (#357). `CompositionPlan.swift` (a pure move out of
  `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, grading GR1) is the plan's Swift side (spec §7.2): `PlanSegment`,
  `PlanRamp`, `PlanTrack`, `PlanInstruction` and `CompositionPlan`; `PlanSpeedRamp.source` is
  its `map` as a `SourceMap`, checked once at decode and not a coding key (SR-20 (c)); `PlanDuck`
  and `ducks` are a speech ducker's own multiplier (format 29, spec §11 AU-113). `AudioProps.swift`
  (a pure move out of `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, road map "audio" AP11's toll) holds the audio group:
  `AudioProps`, `DuckProps` and `CompressorProps`, with format 29's `DuckMode`,
  `DuckProps.mode` / `preRoll` / `hold` and `FadeShape` (and the popups' titles), and format
  30's `LimiterProps` (`audio.limiter`, spec §11 AU-21) with its patch body,
  and format 31's `AudioProps.isolation` (AU-50), and format 32's `eq`, `hum` and `channels`
  (`AudioEQProps.swift`, AU-31, AU-33, AU-34), and format 33's `gate` and `deEsser`

**Frozen files.** `EditorViewController.swift`, `TimelineView.swift`,
`PreviewCanvasView.swift`, `AgentServer.swift` are **frozen at current
size**: anything adding more than ~50 lines goes in an extension file
(`EditorViewController+<Feature>.swift`, `TimelineView+<Feature>.swift`,
`AgentServer+<Feature>.swift`) or a new `…SheetController`, and the frozen
file keeps only the wiring — a stored property, a closure assignment, a
validator arm, a draw call. The pieces extension files build on are therefore
internal, not private. Pitfalls: a selector declared `@objc` on an extension
needs NO forward in the frozen file (a second declaration is an error); a
command whose body sits at the foot of a non-extension feature file carries
its validator arm there too, or the item falls through to the closing
`return true`; `handleEditorCharacter`'s bare-key `switch` matches in SOURCE
order, so a bare `case "x"` goes BELOW any modified `case "x" where …`; and
`handleEditorKey` refuses while a sheet is attached, because a sheet is
window-modal and the preview panel's forwarded keys would otherwise reach
the key map behind it.

- `Playback.swift` (+`Meter`, +`PreviewQuality`, +`Step`, +`Scope`, +`Prefetch`) — one
  `AVPlayer` over the plan's composition; the transport, JKL, the rate KVO; `+Meter` is the level meter, moved out under
  the size rule; `+Scope` also holds `seekFinished()` and `report(_:)`
  (hdr H-3's pure move). `recompose()` re-colours the player's copy of the
  composition without a rebuild (`previewComposition(…, sdrVersion:)`, the
  way Preview Quality does): View ▸ Show SDR Version, spec §11 HD-14. **Only a seek someone ASKED for reports a time**:
  `seek(to:)` is that door, and Playback's own RESTORES — the rebuild's item
  swap and re-seek, the paused refresh's round trip — go through `startSeek`
  silently and report once, only if they come to rest off the last reported
  tick; a scope change seeks through `seekAfterRebuild(to:)`: its time is the
  NEW container's, so the outgoing item is neither sought nor heard and the
  rebuild in flight lands there, heard once (#130, `scope_playhead_probe.py`);
  an asked seek that arrives while a restore is seeking is heard once, when it
  lands; `update`'s same-plan and empty-plan arms discard a rebuild in flight;
  a held scope change whose rebuild fails, or whose new plan is empty, drops
  the item rather than leave the outgoing one, keeps its time and is heard
  once (`endHoldWithoutItem` in `+Scope`, #185; the seek flags are internal
  for `+Scope` alone); `rebuildHop` is the probe's seam, nil in the app, and
  its block takes an error it delivers as the build's failure; `report(_:)` is the one
  caller of `onTimeChanged`. While paused, an observer callback is heard only
  for the tick the player is at or seeking to, and only when it differs from
  the last report — a late callback for a superseded seek or a swapped-out
  item is dropped (#204, #209; `playhead_echo_probe.py` twice·1, pause·1) —
  and every seek's landing reports its rest once when it differs. `+Step`
  also holds the main hop `onMain`. `+Prefetch` is the playing preview's
  graphics prefetch (spec §11 G-36, #127): `syncPrefetch(from:seeking:)`,
  called from the rate KVO, `startSeek` (with the seek's TARGET, never
  `currentTime`, which still reads the player there) and `update`'s
  same-plan arm while playing, and stopped in `invalidate` and `deinit`;
  `recipeKey` is internal for it. `syncPrefetch` first notes activity for
  Background render, and `startBackgroundRender` (G-38) starts a paused pass
  on the composition's grid (`prefetchGrid`), answering why not
  (`.busy` re-arms the clock, `.notNeeded` waits for the next activity). An echoed restore
  moved the playhead (0 and back on every rebuild), and the timeline reveals
  every moved playhead, so a clip drag yanked the view
  (`playhead_echo_probe.py`). **A paused refresh is a one-tick round trip**
  (`refreshPausedFrame`): a zero-tolerance seek to the current time is a
  NO-OP on macOS 26.5.1, so the refresh seeks one tick off and returns; parked
  at the end it rests on the last frame's final tick, because the end tick
  composes black. Do not put a same-time seek back. Preview Quality overrides
  `renderSize` on a copy of the builder's
  `BuiltComposition.videoConfiguration` here (`Playback.previewComposition`,
  static so `phase8_chrome.py` calls it), keeping the
  canvas's EXACT aspect (`m · (w/g, h/g)`, coarser when the divisor does not
  divide `g`, Full for a coprime canvas); `AVPlayerItem.videoComposition` is
  a COPY property, so the setter re-assigns. `makePreviewLayer` is the one
  door to a second `AVPlayerLayer`.
  The item is dropped only for an EMPTY timeline (`plan.duration <= 0`,
  where the transport beeps). Never gate it on the plan's track lists: a
  timeline of only graphics, text, shapes or images has no plan track and
  plays over the builder's placeholder (road map 10 §10.8,
  `media_less_playback_probe.py`).

  `stopped`) is written at its stop. `Slot` lives at the foot of
  `LayerRenderersGraphic.swift` (a pure move under the cap); at 600 lines
  the file's next cut is the background branches.

# app/CLAUDE.md — Swift app rules

Applies to everything under `app/`. Build/verification commands and the FFI
lockstep are in the root `CLAUDE.md`; the full design is
`designs/spec/` (§3–4 the UI, §7.4–7.8 the platform side; its `README.md` is
the index). The
long form of each entry below — why each file is the shape it is, and the
traps its history turned up — is `designs/adr/app-file-history.md` (the
full history, every size toll and measurement, is archived; see its
"Original" line); this file is what governs a file now. Files
are listed by family; a file with a header comment of its own carries its
detail there.

## File map

**The core's edge.**
- `ReelCore.swift` — the **only** home for `rc_*` calls: `ReelProject`
  (handle + lazily decoded `ProjectSnapshot`; `json`, `snapshot` and
  `planJSON` are memoised PER HANDLE, so keep handles rather than minting
  them; so is `sourceMap(_:)`, `rc_project_source_map` decoded and checked
  once per handle and clip, SR-20), timecode, snapping (export presets/sizes/settings are
  `ExportValues.swift`'s, a pure move, HDR H-1), `ReelSpeed.limits` (the
  core's speed range and audio ceiling, typed as `SpeedLimits` in
  `CoreValues.swift` — no Swift file types a speed bound), `ReelColor` (`rc_normalise_color`, G-25), `ReelGraphicPackage` (`rc_graphic_package_write`, G-46; `read`, `rc_graphic_package_read`, G-47), `GraphicLibrary.usage()` (`rc_graphic_library_usage`) and
  `ReelContainer` (`rc_container_*`, a WebM/Matroska file's index,
  #216-R) and `ReelWebM` (`rc_webm_*`, the `av1_webm` writer, spec §11 CX-15) and `ReelHDR10` (`rc_hdr10_peak`, spec §11 HD-6; `av1Peak`,
  `rc_hdr10_av1_peak`, HD-18; `stillPeak`, `rc_hdr10_still_peak`, HD-20), and `GraphicLibrary.imageCache(limit:)`
  (`rc_graphic_image_cache`, G-39); `ReelCoreError`, `Fps.ffiPair` and `ReelTime`'s
  seconds conversions are `CoreValues.swift`'s (G6 phase 5's toll T2 and speed ramps SR4-0,
  pure moves); the typed patches are `TypedPatches.swift`'s (`VideoPatch`,
  `AudioPatch`, `ClipPatch`, the `ActionPatch` extension; a pure move, B73),
  `TextPatch` (with `case`, `words` and `word_style`) is `TextPatch.swift`'s,
  moved out so it could grow, and `ShapePatch` `ShapePatch.swift`'s (a pure
  move, the toll for `ReelColor`). `VideoPatch.color` is a sparse `ColorPatch`
  (`GradeProps.swift`, which holds `ColorAdjust` (moved out of
  `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, grading-2 G2-0) with its neutrality helpers, and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(tone:)`, and the wheels' `ColorWheel`, `ColorWheels`,
  `ColorWheelPatch`, `ColorWheelsPatch`, `ColorWheelKind` and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(wheels:)` (GR-11)); `VideoPatch.curves` is
  `CurveProps.swift`'s `ColorCurvesPatch`, beside `CurvePoint`,
  `CurveDomain`, `CurveChannel`, `CurveBlend` (a channel blended inside an
  action, spec §11 GR-34; `ColorCurves.blends`, never encoded), `ColorCurves` and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(curves:)` (GR-12, the hue curves GR-32; a
  pure move out of `GradeProps.swift`, grading-4 T4-0); `VideoPatch.qualifier` is
  `QualifierProps.swift`'s `ColorQualifierPatch`, beside `ColorQualifier` (its
  `blur`, `blursSelection` and `selectionSigma`, GR-35), `QualifierUniforms`
  (`blurred`, set only by `drawAdjustment`) and the pick's `QualifierSample`
  (GR-13), so a row writes
  only its own key to every selected clip. `word_style` has ONE
  app-side writer, `CaptionLayout.place` (W-10). `ReelAgentSocket` (road map
  14's MC2) wraps `rc_agent_socket_start` / `_release`: `start` throws the
  core's sentence, `release` is the quit's unlink-if-still-ours with no join.
  The `dictionary` extensions on the property types are
  `OpDictionaries.swift`'s (below).
  The graphics engine's wrappers are here too: `GraphicLibrary` (`addFont`,
  `addAsset`, `rasterize`, `families()`; frozen by its first compile,
  rasterize or `families()`) and
  `GraphicModule` (`compile`, `describeJSON`, `svg`; it holds its library
  strongly); their values `GraphicDiagnostic` (with `.error`, `.noModule`
  and `.of(_:)`, the one spelling of a diagnostic made from a message, a
  missing module or a thrown error), `GraphicFailure` (what a
  `diag_out` failure throws; `err_out` stays `ReelCoreError`) and
  `GraphicRaster` are `CoreValues.swift`'s, with `GraphicUsage`, the byte
  bridges `withByteBuffer` and `withMutableByteBuffer` (G-46's toll; never
  `UnsafeMutablePointer(mutating:)`), `SpeedLimits` (a pure move,
  clean-up batch 2), `ReelCoreError` and `Fps.ffiPair` (G6 phase 5's toll), and
  `CoreJSON` (`value`, `snapTicks`: `clipState`'s and `snapCandidates`' JSON
  halves, clean-up round 3's toll; `array`, `overrides`, C1's tolls; `ExportSize.list`,
  `ExportSettings.decoded`, `ReelAV1.Config.decoded`, `withNonNullBytes`, codec-export C5's
  toll), and C1's
  fix-pass moves: `ReelAV1.Config` / `.Color` (an extension of `ReelCore.swift`'s
  `ReelAV1`, whose `rc_av1_*` calls stay there), `GraphicDiagnostic.list(json:)`,
  `GraphicFailure.checkSides`, `SpeedLimits.decoded` and the free `withBytes`.
  `MediaDescriptor`, `MediaOriginal`, `mediaURL(for:)`, `originalURL(for:)`,
  `revealURL(for:)` (the original, else the copy), `isTrashed` and
  `bookmarkString(for:)` are `MediaDescriptor.swift`'s: a `media[]` element
  minus its id, and the media-file resolvers; they call no `rc_*`.
  It is also where the op table is read BACK: `ReelOp.coreNames()` over
  `rc_op_names`, and `ReelOp.coreSchemas()` over `rc_op_schemas` — every
  op's ARGUMENTS as JSON Schema, keyed by op name, which
  `AgentCatalog.opTool` prints for all sixty-four op tools.
  `deinit` frees the Rust allocation. It also holds **the one read of
  `rc_project_apply`'s TWO message channels**, in the header's own order — a
  sentence is a refusal, an error message is invalid input, neither written
  is an identity — answered as the `ReelEdit` below.
- `OpDictionaries.swift` — the `dictionary` extensions on the §5.2
  property types (`CropInsets` … `Gradient`), the model's own key names; a
  pure move out of `ReelCore.swift` (#190, issue batch B52b; road map 14's
  MC2 made the same move as `PropsDictionaries.swift`, and the merge kept
  main's file). With
  `ReelCore.swift` and `ReelOps.swift`, the only files that write an op
  argument. `putNullable` is the one writer of a three-state (`T??`)
  patch key: absent, an explicit null, or the value.
- `ReelOps.swift` — `OpArgs`, `ReelOp` and one typed factory per row of
  `core/src/edit.rs`'s op table, plus a RAW factory beside the typed one at
  each door that takes a CALLER's own object — ELEVEN of them (`setVideoRaw`,
  `setAudioRaw`, `setTextRaw`, `setShapeRaw`, `setClipRaw`,
  `setActionEndRaw`, `addTextClipRaw`, `addShapeClipRaw`, `setCanvasRaw`,
  `addBackgroundRaw`, `addZoomActionRaw`), which takes the
  caller's own object as `Any` — never `[String: Any]`, so a non-object is
  refused by the CORE in the words that name the group — and forwards it;
  there is no untyped op-JSON call site anywhere else. Where only ONE
  argument is the caller's (a colour, a region, a new clip's patch) the typed
  factory DELEGATES to the raw one, mapping its optional explicitly, because
  an `Optional<T>.none` widened to `Any?` is a non-nil `Any` wrapping a nil.
  The typed `setActionEnd` LIFTS every top-level null out of its patch into
  `off` (spec §11 CI-14: a typed `.some(nil)` is a switch turned OFF, kept
  at the end), and a null slot inside `audio.eq` into `audio.eq.<slot>`
  (AU-88); `setActionEndRaw`'s nulls stay removals, which is what
  `clearOps` and every agent call send, and it writes `off` only when non-empty and `schema` only when non-nil
  (the agent door fills it for a graphic end from the module's current
  revision, spec §11 G-34).
  `addZoomActionRaw`'s region is `Any` and not `Any?`: an absent key and an
  explicit null are opposite intentions there, and only the tool can tell
  them apart.
  `scope` is a member folded into `json`; `documentLevelNames` MIRRORS
  `scope.rs`'s `refused_inside` (eight names) so one edit can mix a
  document-level op with scoped ones. A table, with
  `edit.rs`'s size exemption.
- `ReelOpSchema.swift` — what an op TAKES, mirroring what
  `core/src/op_schema.rs` publishes: the `properties` and `required` of one
  op's arguments, which are the two things `AgentServer.tool` takes, and
  `table(from:)`, which reads `rc_op_schemas`' JSON into them (SR4-0's pure
  move out of `ReelCore.swift`, whose `coreSchemas()` keeps the call). Here
  rather than next door for `ReelEdit.swift`'s reason — it names no `rc_*`
  symbol — and `properties` stays `[String: Any]` because a Swift type per
  kind would be another spelling of the table.
- `ReelEdit.swift` — what an op ANSWERS, mirroring `core/src/outcome.rs`:
  `ReelEdit` (`.applied` / `.identity` / `.refused`), `ReelRefusal` (the op
  the core declined and the rule's own sentence, carried verbatim), and the
  fold that applies a LIST — which names no `rc_*` symbol, so it lives here
  and not next door. **Only `.applied` is an undo step**; the other two are
  both "the project did not change" and differ only in what a caller can
  SAY. `.project` is the spelling for a caller that treats a refusal as
  nothing happened (a probe, a live drag), and there is one on
  `ReelEdit?` too for the `try?` probes. In the fold **a refusal does not
  stop the list** — a later op still runs after one, exactly as after an
  identity — and the FIRST refusal is answered only when nothing applied.
- `ProjectSnapshot.swift` · `TextProps.swift` · `MotionProps.swift` ·
  `WordProps.swift` · `MediaSnapshot.swift` · `ActionSnapshot.swift` · `ShapeProps.swift` · `CompositionPlan.swift` · `GradeProps.swift` · `CurveProps.swift` · `AudioProps.swift` — the `Codable`, READ-ONLY mirror
  of spec §5.2 every view draws from. READ-ONLY means never written back as
  is: the stored properties are `var`, so a writer edits a COPY
  (`var s = current(); s.blur = v`) rather than rebuilding one through the
  defaulted memberwise initialiser, which silently drops a field it does not
  spell out; `MotionProps.with(_:)` is motion's per-slot copy (#357). `CompositionPlan.swift` (a pure move out of
  `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, grading GR1) is the plan's Swift side (spec §7.2): `PlanSegment`,
  `PlanRamp`, `PlanTrack`, `PlanInstruction` and `CompositionPlan`; `PlanSpeedRamp.source` is
  its `map` as a `SourceMap`, checked once at decode and not a coding key (SR-20 (c)); `PlanDuck`
  and `ducks` are a speech ducker's own multiplier (format 29, spec §11 AU-113). `AudioProps.swift`
  (a pure move out of `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, road map "audio" AP11's toll) holds the audio group:
  `AudioProps`, `DuckProps` and `CompressorProps`, with format 29's `DuckMode`,
  `DuckProps.mode` / `preRoll` / `hold` and `FadeShape` (and the popups' titles), and format
  30's `LimiterProps` (`audio.limiter`, spec §11 AU-21) with its patch body,
  and format 31's `AudioProps.isolation` (AU-50), and format 32's `eq`, `hum` and `channels`
  (`AudioEQProps.swift`, AU-31, AU-33, AU-34), and format 33's `gate` and `deEsser`
  (`AudioDynamicsProps.swift`, AU-43, AU-45), and format 34's `voice`
  (`VoiceProps.swift`, AU-140), and format 37's `leveller`
  (`AudioDynamicsProps.swift`, AU-66);
  `ProjectSnapshot.swift`'s `TransitionSnapshot.audioShape` is `plus_3db` when absent, and
  `MediaSnapshot.speech` the media's saved spans. `ShapeProps.swift` (a pure
  move out of `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, grading L3) holds the shape group: `StrokeProps`,
  `GradientStop`, `Gradient` and `ShapeProps`. `GradeProps.swift` holds `ColorAdjust` (a pure move out of `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, grading-2 G2-0) beside grading's other value types. `ActionSnapshot.swift` (a pure move out of
  `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, B87) holds `ActionPatch`, `ActionSnapshot` and `ActionGraphicPatch` — an
  end's `graphic.props` and `kinds`, whose `dictionary` sends `props` only. `MediaSnapshot` (a pure move out of
  `ProjectSnapshot.swift`) carries a copy's or an ffmpeg conversion's `original`, and its `name` is
  the one display-name spelling: the original's name when one is recorded. **Its enums decode LENIENTLY**
  — a misspelt kind becomes the first case, a `T??` field a clear — which is
  why a caller-authored object is never decoded through them (below). The
  one exception is `ClipSource`: an unknown `source.kind` THROWS, and
  `ReelProject.snapshot` then falls back to `.empty`, so the WHOLE project
  draws empty with no error. A new source kind in the core is therefore a
  `ClipSource` case in the same phase (road map 10's G2a added `graphic`): no
  agent handler reads a caller-authored OBJECT at all. A scalar enum
  argument is a different thing and several handlers still parse one by name
  (`enumArg` for `add_zoom_action`'s `fit` or an action's `curve`,
  `set_transition`'s `kind` by hand): the
  core refuses those too, and what this rule forbids is decoding a caller's
  object through a lenient type.
  `MotionProps.dictionary` always writes all three keys, `NSNull` for a nil
  slot, because a core patch of `motion` deep-merges — it is the
  APP's writer saying all three slots, not a replace rule, and it is the only
  edge that writes a whole motion. `MotionEdge` also supplies nonpersisted
  zero-duration activity and inactive display/menu titles (E2-27).
  `TextProps.swift` is the text group and `RecipeReveal` (with format version
  9's `textCase` / `words` / `wordStyle`, the recipe's `word` / `wordPop` and,
  since format version 12, `wordGlide` / `wordFill` / `wordDim`), a pure move
  out of `ProjectSnapshot.swift` because a stored property cannot be added
  from an extension. `RecipeReveal` reads and writes its OWN keys — siblings of
  `hash` and `text` in the `text` source — through `init(siblingsOf:)` and
  `encodeSiblings(to:)`, so a new recipe key costs `FrameRecipe.swift`
  nothing; a key spelled other than the snake-case converter spells it
  decodes silently to that key's default (the amount to 1, the rest to nil).
  `ProjectSnapshot+Graphic.swift` mirrors
  `model_graphic.rs`'s `GraphicProps` as `GraphicSnapshot` (`in` is
  `sourceIn`) and `GraphicPropValue` (string, number, bool; anything else
  `.null`), decoded into `ClipSnapshot.graphic`; `props` keys keep the
  module's own spelling (snake-case conversion does not reach a dictionary's
  keys). `WordProps.swift` mirrors `model_words.rs`
  (`TextCase`, `TextWord`, `WordMode`, `ActivePill`, `WordStyle`)
  — `WordStyle.dictionary` writes ALL eight keys (`active_fill` and `pause_dim` since format version 12; `ActivePill.dictionary` writes `glide`), `NSNull` for a nil slot,
  `MotionProps.dictionary`'s rule, because the core deep-merges
  `word_style` — and holds
  what the renderer and the inspector share: `laidContent` (`case` applied —
  every layout and string index is in ITS UTF-16 space, never `content`'s),
  `tokenCount`, `isUntimedPage`, `TextPatch.contentEdit` and
  `InspectorBinding.contentOps` / `ops(textContent:)` — the Content write,
  decided PER CLIP: `words: []` beside the content in one `set_text` only for
  base clips whose count changed, and never `words` in an action end (W-2,
  W-6). It lives there, not in `InspectorPane.swift`, for the size rule.

**The document.**
- `ProjectDocument.swift` (+`DisplayStem`, +`Recording`, +`SelectedAction`, +`Import`, +`Graphics`, +`GraphicFiles`, +`UndoGroup`, +`CacheSaves`, +`Alerts`)
  — NSDocument, `.framejob` package read/write, and the single mutation
  point (see Undo); `applyEdit`'s `.refused` arm beeps and then posts
  `projectDocumentDidRefuse` with the `ReelRefusal` (spec §11 CI-10), which
  the editor forwards to the inspector's refusal strip. Holds the SIX pieces of view state nothing persists —
  playhead, clip selection, in/out range, `selectedMedia`, `nestPath` and
  `selectedAction` — re-clamped by `clampViewState` in that order with the
  scope FIRST, since the selection clamp measures against whatever

validator arm, a draw call. The pieces extension files build on are therefore
internal, not private. Pitfalls: a selector declared `@objc` on an extension
needs NO forward in the frozen file (a second declaration is an error); a
command whose body sits at the foot of a non-extension feature file carries
its validator arm there too, or the item falls through to the closing
`return true`; `handleEditorCharacter`'s bare-key `switch` matches in SOURCE
order, so a bare `case "x"` goes BELOW any modified `case "x" where …`; and
`handleEditorKey` refuses while a sheet is attached, because a sheet is
window-modal and the preview panel's forwarded keys would otherwise reach
the key map behind it.

  phases shipped a section invisible in the app; `editedList` — a write of a
